quote: Remove code scaffolding; session scope is design docs only
defect: A design-only PR carried a go.mod change outside its stated scope from the initial commit until a follow-up removed it.
rule: Before pushing, list every changed file and check each one against the PR's stated scope; remove out-of-scope files from the diff rather than leaving them for a follow-up.
catch_how: Run git diff --stat against main and compare each path with the PR title and summary.
covered_ref: Keep PRs scoped to one logical change

quote: Close IR capability gaps found auditing against the full-spec-union rule
defect: The IR node catalog lacked homes for GraphQL field arguments at non-entry depth, N-ary interface conformance, and XML hints, although the design was declared complete.
rule: Before declaring a model complete, map every construct of every target format to a node or an explicit preservation rule; a construct with no home is a defect in the model, not a later addition.
catch_how: Build a per-format construct checklist and trace each item to a named node or Extensions rule; any item without one fails the audit.
covered_ref: The IR capability surface is complete from day one.

quote: Smithy optionality-vs-nullability was overstated, protobuf `reserved` is not versioning
defect: The initial capability matrix stated several cells incorrectly (overstated or wrong), and roughly 25 cells needed correction after an audit against the specs.
rule: Each capability-matrix cell or spec claim must cite the clause it rests on and be checked against that text before the cell is written.
catch_how: Pick several matrix cells at random and verify each against the spec section it names before merging.
covered_ref: Prefer proving a claim over asserting it

quote: The original prior-art survey of oagen was written from a high-level study;
defect: Prior-art claims about the oagen codebase were written without reading its source, so several were imprecise and one needed rewriting after a source audit.
rule: Verify each claim a design document makes about an external codebase against that codebase's source before merging, and record the file the claim rests on.
catch_how: For each cited behaviour, open the named source file and confirm the behaviour is there before the sentence is written.
covered_ref: Prefer proving a claim over asserting it

quote: and `MessageRef` was referenced but never defined
defect: The design document referenced a type (MessageRef) that it never defined, and messages were embedded by value, contrary to the no-embedded-named-nodes rule.
rule: Before claiming a design document is internally consistent, grep every type name it references and confirm each has a definition in the same document.
catch_how: Extract every backtick-quoted identifier from the document and grep for its definition; report any identifier with no definition.

quote: refactor(compilers): rename frontend→compiler and backend→emitter
defect: The commit that renames the CLI subcommand (a breaking change) carries neither the ! marker in its subject nor a paragraph explaining the break in its body; only the PR title is marked.
rule: A commit that breaks a public interface must carry ! in its subject and explain the break in its body, because the commit message is what a reader of the branch history sees.
catch_how: Run git log on the branch and check that every commit touching a CLI flag, subcommand or exported API is marked breaking and explained.
covered_ref: mark the type with `!`

quote: The planning documents under docs/superpowers/plans/ are local
defect: Local session planning documents were committed to the repository in the initial history and only removed from the index by a follow-up.
rule: Keep agent or session planning and scratch artifacts out of the index: add their path to .gitignore before the first commit that would add them.
catch_how: Run git status and git diff --cached before each commit and read the list of added paths for planning or scratch directories.

quote: fillModelProperties always sets a non-empty WireName, so the Name.Source
defect: The initial commit added fallback branches that no input could reach, and they left the package below the 100% coverage gate.
rule: Before adding a fallback branch, confirm from the producer's invariant that some input reaches it; a branch no input can reach is dead code and must be removed, not covered.
catch_how: Run the coverage profile and check each new branch against the function that populates its input; a branch the profile cannot reach by any test is a deletion candidate.

quote: and the surviving shape depended on branch order.
defect: Reconciling a field redeclared across allOf branches kept the first declaration wholesale, silently dropping type details from later branches and making the result depend on branch order.
rule: When merging duplicate declarations, merge each field by an explicit per-attribute rule and test both declaration orders; never keep one side wholesale.
catch_how: Swap the two branch orders in a test and cmp.Diff the two IR documents; a non-empty diff reveals both the dropped attributes and the order dependence.
covered_ref: Compile the same source twice with the declaration order swapped and `cmp.Diff` the two documents.

quote: a dangling rename target was never reported.
defect: The referential-integrity walk resolved reference-typed values but skipped reference-typed map keys, so a dangling Service.Renames target was never reported.
rule: When a walker follows references, enumerate every position a reference can occupy, including map keys, and test each position with a dangling reference.
catch_how: Plant a dangling reference in each reference-bearing position (value, map key, nested collection) and confirm the verifier reports each one.

quote: Registry-key/ID consistency is checked for Channels, Messages, and
defect: The registry-key/ID consistency check covered only the Types registry, leaving Channels, Messages and Auth unchecked.
rule: When a check is written for one instance of a repeated mechanism, sweep every instance of that mechanism before closing the change.
catch_how: List every registry or map with the same key/ID shape and plant a mismatched key in each one to confirm each is reported.
covered_ref: Sweep every site of the mechanism before closing it.

quote: so the oracle never claims a document is clean when part of it went unchecked.
defect: The bounded reflection walk stopped at its depth cap without reporting, so the oracle could call a document clean while part of it was never checked.
rule: A bounded traversal that stops at its cap must emit a finding; returning as if the traversal completed is a false clean result.
catch_how: Feed a document nested one level past the cap and confirm the checker emits a truncation finding rather than an empty result.

quote: rather than being swallowed by recover() and reported as a
defect: A nil context or empty spec identifier passed to the harness entry point was caught by the recover boundary and reported as a spec-induced compiler panic.
rule: Validate arguments at a public entry point before any recover() boundary, so caller mistakes are never reported as failures induced by the input.
catch_how: Call the entry point with a nil context and with an empty identifier and check that the outcome names the caller error, not a compiler panic.

quote: That blanket equating also masks a real null-vs-[] flip
defect: The round-trip oracle compared structs with cmpopts.EquateEmpty, which hid the null-versus-empty-slice difference that the oracle exists to catch.
rule: Do not use an equivalence option that erases the distinction a check is meant to catch; compare a representation that preserves that distinction.
catch_how: Plant a null-versus-[] flip in a non-omitempty collection and confirm the oracle goes red.
covered_ref: Break what a test claims to catch.

quote: Remove the two crasher seeds: the parser panic and the diagnostic round-trip defects they pin are
defect: Committed reproducers for two known defects were removed to keep CI green, and the known defects were recorded only in a commit message, not in the code or the PR body.
rule: When a known-failing reproducer is removed to keep the suite green, record the deferred defect and its tracking reference in the code and the PR body in the same change.
catch_how: Before removing a failing reproducer, grep the PR body and the touched files for the defect's name; if it is absent, add it there first.
covered_ref: A limitation that is deliberately out of scope must be stated in the code and in the PR body

quote: wrongly reported ir/walk-truncated
defect: The reflection walk depth cap of 256 was below the depth the OpenAPI compiler legitimately produces, so valid deep defaults were reported as truncated.
rule: A bound in a checker must be at least the producer's own bound, derived from the producer's constant and tested at the producer's maximum.
catch_how: Generate the deepest document the producer accepts and run the checker on it; a truncation finding means the checker's bound is too small.

quote: reported as ir/naming-cased.
defect: The naming-neutrality check used unicode.IsUpper, which flagged already-neutral runes with no lowercase form as cased.
rule: When a check approximates a property with a predicate, test the predicate against the producer's exact transformation across the full input domain, not a hand-picked sample.
catch_how: Run the check over every rune the producer can emit and diff its verdict against the producer's own ToLower output.

quote: become package-level seams that default to
defect: The test seams for the harness compile and marshal steps were introduced as package-level variables that tests reassign, which is package-level mutable state.
rule: Inject test seams per instance through a struct field or option, never as package-level variables that tests reassign.
catch_how: Grep the changed packages for package-level var declarations of function type and confirm each one is not reassigned by tests.
covered_ref: no mutable globals

quote: Several error paths were untested: the harness oracle failures
defect: The initial commits were pushed below the 100% statement-coverage gate, with several harness and irverify error paths untested.
rule: Run the full coverage gate before pushing any Go change; a branch that fails the 100% gate is not ready for review.
catch_how: Run make gate locally and confirm it passes on the exact commit being pushed.
covered_ref: Before claiming any Go work done, run and pass the gate

quote: checkRegistryKeys dereferenced Types entries via td.Common(), panicking on a
defect: The verifier, which is specified as report-only, panicked on nil or typed-nil TypeDef entries instead of reporting them.
rule: A checker must return a finding for every input its argument type admits, including nil and typed-nil elements, and must never panic on the data it judges.
catch_how: Fuzz the checker with a nil element placed in every collection the walker visits and confirm it returns findings rather than panicking.

quote: Skip the chmod 0o000 permission test when running as root, where permission
defect: A test that relied on file permission bits failed under a root CI runner, because root bypasses those bits.
rule: A test that depends on OS permission bits or privilege must skip when privilege bypasses them, and must be run once under the CI user.
catch_how: Run the test suite as root in a container and as a normal user, and confirm each permission-dependent test either passes or skips.

quote: have already surfaced a batch of compiler defects, each tracked and fixed in its own change.
defect: The PR body says the surfaced compiler defects were each fixed in their own change, but in this PR the two fuzz reproducers were removed and their fixes had not landed.
rule: A PR description must describe the status of each referenced defect as it stands in the final diff, and must not claim a fix that has not landed.
catch_how: For each claim that a defect is fixed, locate the commit or PR that fixes it before merging.
covered_ref: Prefer proving a claim over asserting it

quote: enrich the input-object and directive fixtures to cover every literal kind (list, object, enum symbol, and
defect: The input-object and directive fixtures did not exercise every literal kind, so the value-lowering branches for some kinds were uncovered until a later fixture was added.
rule: A fixture meant to cover a value domain must enumerate the domain's kinds and confirm each kind appears in the golden output.
catch_how: List every literal kind the lowering switches on and map each to a fixture line that produces it; any kind with no producing line is a gap.

quote: protocompile recovers parser panics internally and returns them as errors, so
defect: The initial commit added a recover and an errParse sentinel that duplicated a guarantee of the parser library and could never fire.
rule: Before adding recover or a defensive error path, check the dependency's contract and confirm some input reaches the path; a path with no reachable input is dead code.
catch_how: Feed the parser a panic-inducing input and observe which layer reports it; if the library already converts it to an error, the local recover is dead.

quote: a descriptor's Options() always returns a materialized options message (empty
defect: Nil-options guards were added around descriptor Options() calls that never return nil, so they were unreachable.
rule: Before guarding a nil return, read the accessor's contract and confirm it can return nil; a guard for a value the accessor never returns is dead code.
catch_how: Check the accessor's implementation or contract for a nil return path, or run the coverage profile to see whether the guard's branch is ever taken.

quote: enrich the corpus with an unmapped well-known type, unsigned/bytes/non-finite
defect: The initial conformance corpus lacked inputs for several lowering branches (unmapped well-known types, unsigned, bytes and non-finite defaults, Empty-input RPCs, deprecated oneof members), so those branches had no golden coverage.
rule: For each branch a lowering takes, the conformance corpus needs at least one input that reaches it; check per-branch coverage, not only per-capability presence.
catch_how: Run the coverage profile over the lowering before pushing and list every uncovered branch; each must map to a corpus input or be removed.

quote: Restores compilers/openapi statement coverage to 100%.
defect: The initial commit shipped reference-resolution branches without tests, leaving compilers/openapi below the 100% coverage gate, while the PR body said the gate held.
rule: Run the coverage gate on the final tree and read the number before writing in a PR body or test plan that it holds; new branches in a lowering path need their tests in the same change.
catch_how: Run make coverage on the initial commit and confirm 100% before claiming it in the test plan.
covered_ref: one uncovered statement fails the build

quote: sameFile compared a $ref's document part to the source purely by basename,
defect: A reference whose document part shared only a basename with the compiled file was treated as a same-file self-reference, so a genuine cross-directory reference resolved wrongly.
rule: When matching a reference's document part to a source file, compare the full path relative to the source; a basename match conflates same-named files in different directories.
catch_how: Add a fixture where dir1/m.yaml references dir2/m.yaml and assert the reference is external, not self-referential.

quote: resolveComponentRef built the resolved ID from the raw $ref pointer text,
defect: The resolved ID was built from the reference's raw pointer spelling, so a non-canonical escape (a bare ~ for ~0) produced an ID matching no interned node.
rule: When a lookup key is derived from a parsed reference, normalise it to the canonical form the definition used, and check every equivalent spelling (escapes, percent-encoding) maps to the same key.
catch_how: Enumerate equivalent spellings of each reference in a fixture (A~B written as A~0B or A~1B) and assert each resolves to the same node with irverify clean.

quote: always resolved to the component's namedTypeID
defect: A discriminator mapping to a bare component name used namedTypeID, which does not match the anonymous ID an empty-named component is interned under, so the mapping dangled.
rule: Derive every target ID for a reference through the same function the definition used; a second shortcut for the same lookup drifts on edge-case names such as the empty string.
catch_how: Target an empty-named component from a discriminator mapping and run irverify's dangling-reference check.

quote: The reference-lowering unification still left two paths that could write a
defect: The earlier change that claimed every reference-lowering path validates its target still left two paths that could write a type ID with no interned node behind it.
rule: When a fix claims to close a class of defects, enumerate every writer of the affected ID or field before claiming the class is closed, and state the enumeration.
catch_how: Grep for every construction site of type and auth IDs and run the dangling-reference oracle on each.
covered_ref: Sweep every site of the mechanism before closing it.

quote: bound keywords unconditionally, not only for in-range values. Morphic re-reads
defect: The library's float64 type-mismatch findings on numeric-bound keywords were suppressed only for in-range values, so a genuinely bad bound still got the library's findings alongside Morphic's own.
rule: When your own reader overrides a second validator's findings, suppress that validator's finding for the whole keyword class, not only for the inputs your reader accepts, or bad inputs get two reports.
catch_how: Feed one out-of-range and one non-numeric bound and count the diagnostics per schema; expect exactly one.

quote: Emit the numeric-bound diagnostic at error severity: it is now the sole report
defect: A non-numeric bound, now the only report of that defect, was emitted at warning severity although it makes the schema invalid.
rule: Assign diagnostic severity from what the input means, and re-check severity whenever a diagnostic becomes the only report for a condition.
catch_how: Assert the severity of the single diagnostic produced for each invalid-input class in the fixture.

quote: now reported and dropped rather than silently accepted as a degenerate
defect: An exclusiveMinimum or exclusiveMaximum in the wrong form for its dialect (a boolean under 2020-12, a number under 3.0) was silently accepted as a degenerate bound instead of being reported.
rule: When a keyword's form depends on the schema dialect, dispatch on the dialect, report the other dialect's form, and never accept it as a valid constraint.
catch_how: Add one 3.0 and one 3.1 fixture each carrying the other dialect's exclusive form and assert a diagnostic on each.

quote: A valid 3.0 boolean exclusive bound, which the library wrongly flags as a numeric type-mismatch, no longer errors.
defect: A valid OpenAPI 3.0 boolean exclusiveMinimum was reported as an error because the library models it as a number and flags it.
rule: Before treating a third-party validator's type finding as a spec error, test it against every valid spelling the spec version allows; a valid input the library mis-types is a false error.
catch_how: Parse a valid 3.0 spec with a boolean exclusiveMinimum and assert zero error diagnostics.

quote: Also close a constraint-loss gap adjacent to the component fix: a $ref to an internal scalar sub-schema that reduces to a shared primitive now carries its
defect: The constraint-preservation fix covered top-level scalar components but not a $ref to an internal scalar sub-schema, which silently dropped its constraints.
rule: When a fix preserves data on one reference path, enumerate every path that reduces to the same node kind (component, $ref, hoisted sub-schema, property) and test each.
catch_how: For each shape that reduces to a primitive, lower a spec with a bound and assert the bound survives in the IR.
covered_ref: Sweep every site of the mechanism before closing it.

quote: This brings compilers/openapi back to 100% statement coverage without
defect: The numeric-BigVal handling shipped without tests for its classifier and guard branches, so the package fell below the 100% coverage gate.
rule: Run the coverage gate on the final tree before pushing; new classifier and guard branches need tests in the same change.
catch_how: Run make coverage on the initial commit and list uncovered statements before opening the PR.
covered_ref: one uncovered statement fails the build

quote: route the OpenAPI and validation-pass diagnostic builders through it, so no
defect: The initial UTF-8 coercion lived only in the OpenAPI compiler's diag.go, so the validation pass's diagnostic builder remained a producer that could emit ill-formed messages.
rule: When a sanitizer or invariant is added at one producer of a type, grep every constructor of that type and route each through the same helper, or enforce the invariant at the type's boundary.
catch_how: Grep for every literal construction of the diagnostic type and confirm each goes through the constructor; run the validation pass over a fixture with a truncated multibyte rune.
covered_ref: Sweep every site of the mechanism before closing it.

quote: so refining a field in a later allOf branch was reported as a contradiction.
defect: Conflict detection classified enums, consts, unions and external types as structurally incompatible with a scalar, so satisfiable narrowings in a later allOf branch produced false conflict warnings.
rule: When a conflict detector declares two types incompatible, classify each kind positively as structural or scalar, and test the satisfiable narrowings (enum, const, union, alias) to confirm they produce no diagnostic.
catch_how: Narrow a string field by an enum, a const and a [string, integer] union in a later branch and assert zero diagnostics.

quote: Reconciliation also took the first branch's constraint set wholesale, so
defect: Reconciliation adopted the first branch's constraint set as a whole, so keywords declared only by a later branch (minLength, pattern) were dropped without a diagnostic.
rule: When merging two keyword sets, merge per key and test complementary keys from each side in both orders; adopting one side wholesale silently drops the other side's keys.
catch_how: Use a two-branch allOf with disjoint keywords (maxLength in one, minLength and pattern in the other) and diff the merged keys in both branch orders.

quote: alongside allOf rather than inside a branch.
defect: The diagnostic said allOf branches even for a property declared alongside allOf rather than inside a branch, so its text misdescribed the source position it fired on.
rule: Make a diagnostic's text describe the syntactic position it fires on; when one check runs at several positions, parameterise the wording and assert it per position.
catch_how: Trigger the same conflict at a branch-level property and at a sibling property and read both messages.

quote: The doc comments no longer describe a contradictory constraint as unsatisfiable: maxLength 10 and
defect: The initial commit called contradictory constraint keywords unsatisfiable, but maxLength 10 and 20 intersect to 10; only the arbitrary winner the merge keeps is the real problem.
rule: Before writing unsatisfiable or contradiction in a diagnostic or comment, compute the intersection of the exact pair it fires on, and claim unsatisfiability only when that intersection is empty.
catch_how: For each diagnostic message, take the keyword pair it fires on and check the intersection with a table test.

quote: The merge is now independent of branch order.
defect: The PR body says the constraint merge is independent of branch order, while the same body says a contradictory keyword keeps an arbitrary source-order winner, which is order-dependent.
rule: Before writing that a merge is independent of order, run the conflicting-key case in both orders; a merge that keeps a source-order winner is order-dependent.
catch_how: Run a two-order diff on a branch pair with a conflicting maxLength.
covered_ref: Order-dependence needs a two-order diff.

quote: - Fix typesConflict to only flag structural-vs-scalar conflicts, not
defect: typesConflict flagged an opaque scalar (custom format) against its primitive as a conflict, which the never-guess principle does not allow.
rule: A conflict detector should flag only the pairs it can prove incompatible; for a type it cannot see into, such as an opaque scalar, report nothing rather than guess.
catch_how: Redeclare a custom-format scalar as its base primitive in a fixture and assert zero diagnostics.

quote: - Soften 'intersected' wording in constraintsConflict docstring to
defect: The constraintsConflict docstring said constraints were intersected, while one-sided keywords are adopted, not merged.
rule: Describe a merge in its doc comment by what it does to each key (adopted, merged or dropped), not with a set-theory term the code does not implement.
catch_how: Read the doc comment against each branch of the function, including the one-sided case.

quote: It reported 100% statement coverage, but almost all of it came
defect: The ir package's 100% statement coverage came almost entirely from two broad round-trip tests, so adding omitempty to Property.Required or TypeRef.Nullable passed the suite.
rule: Treat statement coverage as a reachability measure, not an assertion measure: mutate each serialized tag or invariant and confirm a test reddens before trusting a green coverage number.
catch_how: Add omitempty to Property.Required and to TypeRef.Nullable one at a time and run go test ./ir; expect red each time.
covered_ref: Break what a test claims to catch.

quote: Several tests survived the file-per-source consolidation sitting in a file
defect: The file-per-source consolidation left tests in a file that shared their topic but not the defining file of the unexported function they call.
rule: After reorganising tests by source file, map each test's called unexported symbols to their defining file and assert they match, rather than matching by topic.
catch_how: For each test, list the unexported identifiers it calls and compare with the file that defines them.

quote: and restore package_test (external) for the files whose remaining tests
defect: Consolidation folded external-package test files into internal-package targets even where their tests touched only the public API.
rule: Keep a test in the external test package unless it needs unexported identifiers, and check the package clause of every test file a move touches.
catch_how: Grep the package clauses before and after a file move and diff them.
covered_ref: external test packages (`package foo_test`) preferred

quote: 3200-line document took 41 seconds.
defect: Each mapping read recomputed the full merge-key closure, so a 3200-line merge-chain document took 41 seconds and the scan turned a crash into a hang.
rule: When a helper materialises an expansion (aliases, merge keys, includes), cache it and time the largest pathological fixture before pushing; per-read recomputation is quadratic on chains.
catch_how: Time a 3200-line merge-chain fixture and add a timing guard to the test suite.
covered_ref: Bounded everything.

quote: expanded as merges, which reported a cyclic $ref in documents that parse
defect: Quoted '<<' keys and alias-valued keys were expanded as merge keys, reporting a cyclic $ref for documents that parse cleanly and never reach the resolver.
rule: When a check mirrors a parser's special syntax, test the non-special spellings (quoted, aliased, explicitly tagged) and confirm the check does not fire on them.
catch_how: Parse each spelling of the special key and assert the check's output matches the library's decoded view.

quote: but memoization and a recursion depth cap are unsound together: a node first
defect: The ref-collection walk was recursive with a depth cap and memoization; a node first reached near the cap was truncated, then skipped on a shallow revisit, silently dropping the refs beneath it.
rule: Do not memoise a result computed under a truncation bound, since a truncated result depends on the entry path; cache only complete results, or use a worklist with visited sets instead of a bound.
catch_how: Walk a deep chain entered deepest-first and shallowest-first and diff the collected refs.
covered_ref: Order-dependence needs a two-order diff.

quote: The mapping view added for alias and merge-key resolution reused maxCycleDepth
defect: The merge-expansion bound reused the recursion-depth limit (10000), letting a 180 KB spec with a 6000-level merge chain retain 2.2 GB.
rule: Give each materialised resource its own named bound sized to its cost; do not borrow a bound from a different quantity such as recursion depth because the number is already in the file.
catch_how: Run the scanner on a 6000-level merge chain and measure retained heap against input size.
covered_ref: Bounded everything.

quote: Truncation is per node, not per scan. An earlier form of this latched a flag
defect: An earlier truncation design latched one flag that stopped all expansion for the scan, so one over-deep merge chain ahead of a real cycle could disable the cycle check.
rule: A resource bound must degrade only the item that hit it; a scan-wide latch lets one crafted input switch off the protection for every other input.
catch_how: Place an over-deep merge chain before a real cycle in a fixture and assert the cycle is still reported as an error.

quote: future dependency bump at the wrong model to re-verify against.
defect: The isMergeKey comments named yaml.v3's isMerge as the model to re-verify against, though speakeasy is the reader of these documents.
rule: A comment that names the reference model a check mirrors must name the consumer that actually reads the input, so a dependency bump re-verifies the right code.
catch_how: For each mirror comment, confirm the named model is the one whose behaviour the code copies.

quote: The ref-collection walk's dispatch gains an explicit roleSchemaList case and a
defect: The walk's role dispatch had no case for the schema-list role, so that role fell through to whichever node kind the switch handled instead of failing loudly.
rule: Dispatch over a closed set of roles or kinds with an explicit case for each member and a panicking default, so a new member fails loudly instead of being handled as another kind.
catch_how: Add a role constant without a case and run the walk tests; expect a panic, not a silent walk.
covered_ref: type switches carry a `default`

quote: a shared set let the first role mark it seen so the second skipped it — dropping
defect: A single visited set shared across walk roles let the first role mark an anchored $ref node as seen, so the second role skipped it and dropped the node the cycle chain needed.
rule: When one graph node can be read under several interpretations (role, kind), key the visited set by (node, interpretation); a shared set lets the first reading hide the second.
catch_how: Drive one anchored node into two roles and assert both roles visit it.

quote: The cycle pre-scan read a mapping that declares the same key twice as first-key-wins.
defect: The cycle pre-scan resolved a repeated mapping key to its first value while the decoder it protects uses the last, so a self-referential redeclaration was missed and reached the resolver's stack overflow.
rule: When a pre-parse check reads a structure the library later decodes, match the library's duplicate-key and precedence rules, and add a fixture where the duplicate changes the verdict.
catch_how: Build a duplicate-key fixture whose last value is the cyclic one and assert the scan agrees with the decoded tree.

quote: `unmarshal` has guarded the third-party parser since the first crash fix, but
defect: A recover barrier guarded the parser call but not the ResolveAllReferences call into the same library, so a nil dereference in the resolver escaped Compile as a panic.
rule: When a panic barrier wraps one call into a third-party library, list every other call into that library and barrier each one, or barrier at the package boundary.
catch_how: Grep for every call into the library's package and check each runs under a recover, or fuzz every entry point with malformed references.
covered_ref: Sweep every site of the mechanism before closing it.

quote: 💘 Generated with Crush
defect: The PR body carried a tool-generated attribution line instead of a self-contained description of the problem and change.
rule: Keep PR descriptions free of tool-generated attribution or session artifacts; state the problem, the change and the reason in the body's own terms.
catch_how: Read the PR body against the description rules before opening the PR.
covered_ref: No LLM/session artifacts, no internal audit/finding IDs

quote: unreachable from a parsed document, so nothing in the existing tests
defect: The PR shipped defensive alias-weigher guards that no parsed input can reach, so the 100% statement-coverage gate failed until hand-built-node tests were added.
rule: Before pushing, run the coverage gate on the final tree, and give every defensive guard that no parsed input reaches a test built from hand-constructed inputs.
catch_how: Run scripts/check-coverage.sh on the branch and list the uncovered statements before opening the PR.
covered_ref: Coverage is a gate at exactly 100%, not a target.

quote: pinned a 40-level × 2-way fan-out as **clean**.
defect: A pre-existing test pinned a 40-level alias fan-out as clean although that document exhausts memory at 18 levels, so the test asserted a live crash as correct.
rule: Before accepting a test's expected verdict for a fixture, run the fixture under the same time and memory bounds the code claims to enforce; a fixture that itself crashes cannot be the clean case.
catch_how: Run the pinned input under a memory limit (ulimit -v or a bounded harness) and confirm it completes before asserting its verdict.

quote: The two constants bounding alias expansion were sized against invented
defect: Both amplification bounds were tuned against documents the author wrote, so the constants were never checked against any published spec.
rule: Calibrate every heuristic limit against a real corpus and record the measured worst case and margin; a limit tuned only on documents you wrote proves nothing about real inputs.
catch_how: Measure the limit against the worst real-world input in a corpus and report the margin before merging.

quote: The doc comments on the amplification constants had grown to the point of
defect: Doc comments on the amplification constants ran to about 92 lines on one constant and restated the same calibration figures several times.
rule: Count the words of each doc comment you add or edit against the 100-word cap, and state each fact once.
catch_how: Run go test ./internal/archtest -run TestDocComments and read its over-cap list before pushing.
covered_ref: Doc comments: 100 words at most.

quote: spellings, so a target spelling nullability as a union null branch lost the bit

defect: CLAUDE.md's package-layout tree omitted real packages and told the reader to write an import-graph test that already existed, sending contributors to rebuild enforced mechanisms.
rule: When a doc describes a repository layout or a test mechanism, derive the description from the tree or from the enforcing test rather than restating it, and check that every named package and mechanism exists.
catch_how: Run git ls-files '*/*.go' | xargs -n1 dirname | sort -u and diff it against every package list the doc names.
covered_ref: Prefer the command that derives a number, or omit it.

quote: The pre-flight command list was the consequential one: it omitted the coverage
defect: The pre-flight checklist omitted the exact-100% coverage gate, so a green go test was presented as evidence the gate would pass.
rule: A pre-flight checklist must be the CI gate's exact command list derived from the workflow file and Makefile, not a remembered subset of it.
catch_how: Diff the checklist's commands against the steps in .github/workflows/gate.yml and the Makefile gate target.
covered_ref: Before claiming any Go work done, run and pass the gate:

quote: is what left the identical defect standing in the inline-position hoist.
defect: The pointer-collision fix was scoped to the union lowering where it was noticed, leaving the same defect standing in the inline-position hoist.
rule: When a fix repairs a collision or other defect, sweep every site that runs the same mechanism (every place that mints a node at a source pointer) and fix or justify each before the PR opens; never scope the fix to the site where it was first noticed.
catch_how: Grep for every constructor call of the mechanism and run the two-order diff on a fixture that reaches each call site.
covered_ref: Sweep every site of the mechanism before closing it.

quote: Promoting the naming grammar is not behaviour-neutral, since the three copies disagree and at most one
defect: The first design draft called promoting the naming grammar behaviour-neutral, but the three copies disagree, so at most one survives unchanged.
rule: Before calling a refactor behaviour-neutral, confirm the copies being unified agree on the input domain; unifying divergent copies changes output and needs its own fixture-backed decision.
catch_how: Run each copy over one shared set of identifiers, including punctuated ones, and diff the outputs before writing 'neutral'.
covered_ref: Probe, don't read.

quote: CLAUDE.md carry a package-layout tree that this effort invalidates, and
defect: A restructuring that moved packages left two documents, the architecture doc and CLAUDE.md, carrying a package-layout tree the change had invalidated.
rule: When a change moves packages or changes a shape a document diagrams, grep every document that diagrams it and update each in the same change.
catch_how: grep -rn each moved package path across docs/ and CLAUDE.md before pushing, and reread any tree that still lists the old layout.

quote: Also unblocks the naming-divergence defect, which had been made to wait
defect: The plan made a standalone naming defect wait on the larger programme that would fix it, contradicting the reason the defect was filed separately.
rule: When a plan records a blocking edge, check the edge against the stated reason the item was split out; an edge that makes a standalone defect wait on a larger programme contradicts why it was split.
catch_how: For each blocked-by edge, read the issue's reason for separation and confirm the blocker is not needed for the item's own fix.

quote: canonicalWords treated only _, - and space as separators, so every other
defect: The canonical-name splitter recognised only underscore, hyphen and space, so every other punctuation character survived into the canonical word sequence.
rule: When a contract defines a word sequence by character class, implement the separators as the complement of the word class (every character that is not a letter or digit) rather than an enumerated list of the examples seen.
catch_how: Fuzz the canonicalizer with random printable punctuation and assert every output is a sequence of words.

quote: checkNaming tested lowercase-idempotence
defect: The naming verifier checked only lowercase idempotence, so it accepted every punctuated or mis-segmented canonical because all of those spellings were lowercase.
rule: Give a verifier the inputs its contract forbids, not only the cases the current corpus produces; a check that passes every spelling it is meant to reject tests nothing.
catch_how: Plant each forbidden spelling (punctuation, dotted, bracketed) into the verifier's input and confirm a violation is reported.
covered_ref: Break what a test claims to catch.

quote: The corpus had the same blind spot: no committed spec named anything with
defect: No committed conformance spec used punctuation in any name, so the corpus sweep could never exercise the naming failure it was meant to catch.
rule: Before relying on a corpus sweep to exercise a check, confirm a committed fixture reaches the input class the check guards; if none does, add one.
catch_how: grep the fixtures for the input class (for example punctuation in names) and confirm a hit before trusting a clean sweep.
covered_ref: A corpus shares the blind spots of the code it covers

quote: pass.Validate read a subtype's Base one hop, so a discriminator hierarchy whose
defect: pass.Validate read a subtype's base one hop, so a valid discriminator hierarchy whose subtype annotates its base reference was reported as an error.
rule: When a field can name an alias, make every consumer read through the alias chain (bounded) rather than one hop, and test each consumer with an annotated-alias input, not only hand-built documents.
catch_how: Compile a spec whose subtype base is annotated through an alias and run pass.Validate on the compiled output.

quote: not run the pass and the pass's tests build documents by hand, so it is covered
defect: The subtype defect was invisible to both suites: the compiler corpus never ran the pass, and the pass's tests built their documents by hand.
rule: A check that runs is not a check that reaches: when a consumer's inputs come from another stage, add at least one test that feeds it that stage's real output.
catch_how: Run the consumer on the compiler's output for each committed spec, not only on hand-built documents, and confirm the test reaches the defective path.
covered_ref: A check that runs is not a check that reaches.

quote: ir.Scalar.Base was documented as
defect: The Scalar.Base doc comment said the field names a primitive or another scalar, a contract that hoisted aliases had never obeyed.
rule: When a doc comment restricts what a field may hold, check every producer of that field against the restriction, and correct the comment when no producer obeys it.
catch_how: grep every assignment to the field and check each against the comment; run a fixture with a hoisted alias and inspect the field.

quote: An outside $ref can name a branch pointer, so the composition and hoistSubSchema
defect: Two lowerings that can intern the same branch node derived different name hints, so the document depended on which declaration lowered first.
rule: When two code paths can each intern the same node, derive every attribute they set from one shared source (the reference target), and cover the pair with a two-order test.
catch_how: Run the two-order diff on a fixture where an external reference names the shared node.
covered_ref: Order-dependence needs a two-order diff.

quote: An allowlist entry matched as a segment prefix, and compilers/openapi is allowed
defect: An allowlist entry matched by segment prefix, so compilers/graphql passed as allowed to import the compilers contract package, leaving the no-cross-compiler rule unenforced.
rule: When a rule's allowlist matches by prefix, plant an import from a sibling that shares the prefix and confirm it is rejected; make matches exact unless a wildcard is written.
catch_how: Plant an import from a sibling package whose path begins with an allowed entry and run the architecture test.
covered_ref: Break what a test claims to catch.

quote: The skip decision for a subdirectory carrying its own rule compared basenames
defect: A subdirectory with its own rule was skipped by basename at any depth, so a nested irtest or irverify directory was audited by nothing while the coverage check still counted it as covered.
rule: When an audit skips entries by name, match the full path, and plant a same-named directory at another depth to confirm the audit still reaches it.
catch_how: Plant ir/sub/irtest importing testify and confirm the architecture test reports it.
covered_ref: Break what a test claims to catch.

quote: OpenAPI 3.1 allows keywords beside a $ref. On an allOf branch they were all
defect: Keywords written beside a $ref on an allOf branch, vendor extensions included, were discarded with no diagnostic.
rule: For every schema position that can carry a $ref with sibling keywords, route the lowering through the shared path, and confirm with a fixture that writes a sibling keyword at each position that none disappears.
catch_how: Write description, minProperties and an x-vendor extension beside a $ref at every position and diff the IR for dropped keys.
covered_ref: Lossless by default, lowered late.

quote: Both documents asserted the defects in the present tense
defect: The design and plan documents described fixes that had shipped as still-open defects, in the present tense.
rule: When a change ships work that a design or plan document lists as pending, update that document in the same change and reread its present-tense claims against the code.
catch_how: After landing, grep the design and plan docs for each landed item and check each statement about it against the tree.

quote: nodeToRaw returned nil both for an absent construct and for one whose YAML
defect: A diagnostic announced that a construct was kept verbatim under Unmodeled even when its YAML-to-JSON conversion had failed and nothing was written.
rule: Emit a 'kept' or 'dropped' diagnostic only after the write it describes has succeeded, and make a failed conversion return a distinguishable error rather than a nil that also means absent.
catch_how: Feed a payload that fails conversion (a non-string mapping key, or .nan) and assert the diagnostic set matches what the output actually contains.

quote: header lowered as if it had no schema at all: the type became t/prim/any and
defect: A header declared with a content map lowered as untyped, dropping its schema type, constraints and xml hints without a diagnostic.
rule: When a construct has two source spellings, lower both and compare them on one fixture; a fallback branch must not run silently for the spelling it was not written for.
catch_how: Write the same schema in both spellings, lower each, and diff the IR; any difference is a finding.
covered_ref: Probe, don't read.

quote: It did share the adjacent one, so
defect: The request-parameter path shared an adjacent gap, silently taking the first of several media types, which the header fix had not covered.
rule: When fixing a gap at one position, grep the sibling positions that read the same keyword for the same gap, and fix or justify each before pushing.
catch_how: grep for every reader of the keyword (content, schema) and run the failing fixture through each reader.
covered_ref: Sweep every site of the mechanism before closing it.

quote: partEncodings enumerated the parts from the body
defect: A multipart body that composes its schema through allOf lost its whole encoding block with no diagnostic, because part enumeration read only the node's own properties.
rule: When an enumeration reads a node's own children, check whether that node can be a composition whose children live in referenced or mixin schemas, and test the enumeration with a composed input.
catch_how: Add a fixture whose body is an allOf of a $ref and diff its encoding block against the spelling where the properties are declared in place.

quote: named a property that exists nowhere
defect: Keying encoding entries by a property ID re-derived from the composed node's pointer would name a property the IR never holds, leaving a dangling reference.
rule: Key a reference by the identifier the target actually stores, looked up from the target, never by re-deriving it from a pointer that may not own the target.
catch_how: Assert every key in the emitted map resolves to a PropID present in the registry.

quote: An ID reached through a JSON Schema $anchor was derived from the anchor name as
defect: An ID derived from a $anchor name was built as though the name were a source pointer, and nothing checked that IDs obey the grammar that builds them.
rule: For every derived identifier with a grammar, add a verifier check that rejects any value the grammar cannot produce, and a check that the identifier agrees with the coordinate recorded beside it.
catch_how: Plant an ID with a dropped separator and an ID whose path disagrees with its recorded pointer, and confirm the verifier reports both.

quote: the resolver library failing rather than from any check of its own.
defect: The refusal of an anchor reference came from the resolver library failing, not from a check in the compiler, so a library that began resolving anchors would silently reinstate the bad derivation.
rule: Enforce your own input boundary with an explicit check rather than relying on a dependency to reject the input, since the dependency may later accept it.
catch_how: Stub the dependency to accept the input and confirm the compiler's own check still refuses it.

quote: checkNaming asserted that a canonical name carries no casing and is made of
defect: The canonical-name check verified casing and character set but not word segmentation, so 'foo2bar' and 'foo_2_bar' both passed.
rule: A verifier for a grammar must check every property the grammar defines (casing, character set, segmentation), and each property needs its own rejecting example.
catch_how: Plant one example per grammar property the contract states and confirm the verifier rejects each.

quote: the second node simply overwrites the first in
defect: A registry keyed by source coordinate let two distinct coordinates that derived the same ID overwrite each other silently, and no structural check saw the loss.
rule: Any map keyed by a derived identifier must refuse a second distinct source key that derives the same identifier, because overwrite is silent data loss.
catch_how: Plant two coordinates that derive one ID and assert the registry refuses the second, while one coordinate interned twice still succeeds.

quote: MissingCells could not notice the absence: it looked complete over a set of
defect: The annotation-retention grid had no axis for a carrier position, so its completeness check passed over cells it could not express.
rule: Before trusting a completeness check over a grid, confirm each axis can name the cells it claims to cover; an axis that cannot express a position makes 'complete' vacuous.
catch_how: Remove one carrier kind's cell from the grid and confirm MissingCells reports it.

quote: It filtered in place through parts[:0], so the returned slice shared a backing
defect: dedupeParts filtered in place, so its returned slice aliased its input and would silently rewrite a caller that read the input again.
rule: Build a filtered slice in a fresh allocation when the input may be read again; in-place filtering through s[:0] aliases the input.
catch_how: Call the helper and assert the input slice is unchanged afterwards.
covered_ref: copy slices/maps at API boundaries

quote: keepKeyword took a label alongside its keyword and was called three times with
defect: keepKeyword took a label parameter that every caller set equal to the keyword, so the parameter carried no choice.
rule: Remove a parameter that every call site sets to the same value, or to a value derivable from another argument, in the change that introduces the callers.
catch_how: grep the call sites of the function and check whether any argument position varies.

quote: The branch could not be reddened by any input, which is the shape this repository treats as worse than no branch at all
defect: reverseNode carried a case that no parser output reaches, so no test could redden it.
rule: Delete a branch that no input can reach and record the fact in the comment, rather than keeping a branch no test can exercise.
catch_how: Mutate the branch to return a wrong value and check whether any test or fixture reddens; if none can, the branch is dead.
covered_ref: A check that runs is not a check that reaches.

quote: said "not yet implemented" while four rows were marked landed
defect: A document's status line said work was not yet implemented while four rows were marked landed in the same document.
rule: Derive a document's status line and row counts from its row markers, or update the status line in the same change that marks a row.
catch_how: grep the doc's status text, count the landed markers, and compare.
covered_ref: Derive counts; never maintain them.

quote: the webhook group named itself with a
defect: The webhook group was named with a bare Source and no canonical words, leaving every emitter to segment it itself.
rule: When a new verifier check lands, run it over the full committed corpus before merging and treat each new violation as a finding in the compiler output it names.
catch_how: Run the harness sweep with the new check enabled and read every violation it reports before merging.

quote: settled the wrong half: it recorded an invented name as one the API author
defect: A prior fix recorded a compiler-synthesized group name as a source-declared name, misstating its provenance.
rule: A name the compiler synthesizes belongs in the hint channel, never in the declared-source field, even when a fix is only meant to add canonical words.
catch_how: For each synthesized identifier, check whether any source spelling exists; if none does, the value must go in the hint field.
covered_ref: Heuristics are policy, not semantics.

quote: #184 had already framed that as a decision wanting its own
defect: A change touched a line whose decision was already recorded in an issue and settled it differently without consulting that issue.
rule: When a change is forced onto a line, search the tracker for that file or symbol before choosing, and either follow the recorded decision or say explicitly why you depart from it.
catch_how: Run gh issue list --search with the file or symbol before editing a line that a check made fail.
covered_ref: A line you were forced onto may already have a decision recorded.

quote: a golden shows the name moving between two fields
defect: A conformance golden recorded a value whose field placement was a design decision, without asserting which field was right, so the decision could drift unseen.
rule: When a golden records a value whose placement is a decision, add an assertion on the chosen field; a golden records what happened, not what is correct.
catch_how: Revert the decision and confirm the explicit assertion, not only the golden diff, goes red.

quote: The doc comment said the error return "never reports a spec-level problem", and three of its four paths are
defect: A doc comment claimed an error return never reports a spec-level problem, though three of its four paths are reachable from source documents.
rule: Check a doc comment's absolute claim (never, always) against every return path; enumerate the reachable paths or drop the absolute.
catch_how: List each error return and trace whether a source document can reach it; keep the absolute only if none can.

quote: "load and scan sit on the entry side, imported only by openapi.go"
defect: A design document stated a package's import edges from a file-level reading, missing three real dependencies.
rule: Derive a design document's dependency claims from the import graph (go list -deps or the archtest rules), not from file names or from how the code was meant to look.
catch_how: Run go list -deps for each package named in the claim and compare the edges before writing it down.
covered_ref: Prefer proving a claim over asserting it

quote: packages now, so it found nothing in the working tree.
defect: The tier-0 diagnosis command read the working tree, where the files it named no longer existed, so it returned nothing and proved nothing.
rule: A diagnosis or check command must read the revision it describes and be run once against a known-positive input; an empty result from a stale path is not evidence.
catch_how: Run the command against a revision where the named files exist and confirm it prints output before trusting an empty result.
covered_ref: A check that runs is not a check that reaches.

quote: MergeDepthLimit compared itself to maxCycleDepth, which lives in the
defect: A doc comment pointed at a constant in a package above the reader's, so the reader could not resolve the reference.
rule: A doc comment should name only symbols resolvable from its own package; when a bound lives elsewhere, name the local bound that holds the same value.
catch_how: For each identifier in a doc comment, check that it resolves in that package's scope.

quote: `multipleOf`'s conflict formatter took a keyword parameter it was only ever
defect: The multipleOf conflict formatter took a keyword parameter that every caller set to one value.
rule: Remove a parameter that every call site sets to the same value, or to a value derivable from another argument, in the change that introduces the callers.
catch_how: grep the call sites of the function and check whether any argument position varies.

quote: Also correct the type's own doc comment, which claimed the context is
defect: The lowering context type's doc comment said the context is passed and copied by value, though nothing passed it yet; it was only held by the lowerer.
rule: Before writing a doc comment that says how a value flows (passed, copied, stored, shared), grep its call sites and describe the flow the code has today, not the one a later change will add.
catch_how: grep for every use of the type and read each one; check each verb in the comment (passed, copied) against those uses.

quote: Naming the type ctx gave this package three meanings for one identifier:
defect: The lowering context type was first named ctx, which collided with the context.Context parameter and an existing local, so one identifier had three meanings in one package.
rule: Before naming a package-level type or variable, grep the package for that identifier and reject any name already bound to another meaning, including parameters and locals.
catch_how: grep -rnw over the package for the candidate name and inspect every hit before choosing the name.

quote: Three call sites still named the moved functions by their old unqualified
defect: After eight functions moved to a new package, three call sites and their comments still named them by their old unqualified names.
rule: After moving or renaming symbols, grep the whole tree, comments and tests included, for the old unqualified names; a compile check does not catch stale comment references.
catch_how: grep the old identifiers across the tree after the move and expect zero hits outside the new package.

quote: It credited the directory guard
defect: sameFile's comment credited a directory check with distinguishing two paths, but the equality alone already did so and the guard was redundant.
rule: A doc comment that credits a specific check with a behaviour must be tested by removing that check and seeing whether the behaviour changes; if it does not, state what the check actually does.
catch_how: delete the guard, run the test for the case the comment names; if nothing changes, the comment is wrong.

quote: run against every compilers/ file it listed the
defect: The documented derivation command was run over every compilers/ file, so it listed another branch's copies of openapi files as though they belonged to the compiler the doc discusses.
rule: A derivation command written into a design doc must be scoped to the branch and paths it describes, and run on that branch before it is quoted.
catch_how: run the documented command on the intended branch and on one other branch; the outputs must differ only where intended.
covered_ref: Prefer the command that derives a number, or omit it.

quote: The note on accumulate.go said the upper layer reached schema.go for this
defect: A note said the upper layer reached schema.go for one thing only, but three symbols still crossed that boundary, so the note overstated how decoupled the layers were.
rule: When a note says a dependency has been removed or narrowed, re-derive the remaining references from the import or call graph and list what is left, not only what was removed.
catch_how: list every remaining cross-file reference with a grep or type-checker query and compare the result to the note's wording.

quote: Also correct diag's own comment, which still called it the single
defect: diag's doc comment still described it as the one primitive that constructs a Provenance after that construction had moved to provenanceAt.
rule: When a helper's job moves to another function, grep the doc comments of the package for the old job and rewrite every claim that still assigns it to the helper.
catch_how: grep the package comments for the old responsibility's wording after the move and read each hit against the code that now does the work.

quote: Coverage was complete and the guarantee was still unnamed
defect: The provenance guarantees were covered by line coverage but had no test named for them, so a change to the source index or pointer would fail no test by name.
rule: Line coverage is not evidence that a guarantee is tested: for each invariant a helper provides (stamped location, single spelling of a source index), add a test that fails by name when that step is removed.
catch_how: remove the source-index assignment in the helper and check that a test named for the guarantee reddens.
covered_ref: Plant the defect and watch it go red.

quote: registeredNode's contract credited intern with recording a pointer's ID
defect: registeredNode's contract credited intern with recording the pointer's ID, though intern had been deleted and the registry does the recording.
rule: When deleting a forwarding function, grep the package's doc comments for its name and rewrite every claim that depended on it.
catch_how: grep -rn for the deleted function's name in comments after the deletion and expect no hits.

quote: Recording that #175 runs after #176 on the two issues left the planning
defect: Recording a new sequence on the issues left four planning-doc locations stating the old order, including the blocked-by column and the critical-path diagram.
rule: When a decision changes a sequence or dependency, grep every planning document for each affected item and update every mention in the same change.
catch_how: after editing, grep the item numbers across docs/ and read each hit for the order it states.
covered_ref: Sweep every site of the mechanism before closing it.

quote: Four of the six converted functions still described themselves as
defect: Four of six functions converted from recording to returning diagnostics still described themselves as reporting or recording, so their comments contradicted the new contract.
rule: When a function changes from performing an effect to returning its result, rewrite every doc comment in the package that describes the old effect, verb by verb.
catch_how: after the change, grep the converted functions' comments for record, emit, report and announce and read each hit against the new return.

quote: Dropping the operation-extension diagnostic
defect: Converting a wrapper to return its diagnostics left each caller free to drop the operation-extension warning while no test failed.
rule: When a function starts returning diagnostics to its caller, add a test per caller that fails when the caller drops them, and run that mutation before pushing.
catch_how: delete each caller's append of the returned diagnostics in turn and confirm a test named for that diagnostic reddens.
covered_ref: Plant the defect and watch it go red.

quote: It asserted that some degraded
defect: The test asserted only that some construct was degraded; it passed by accident because the spec had one bad extension, and it did not name the extension.
rule: A test that checks for a diagnostic must assert the subject the message names (the offending key or pointer), not a generic outcome an unrelated cause could also produce.
catch_how: add a second unrelated degraded construct to the fixture and confirm the assertion still identifies which one is reported.

quote: Three of the four converted wrappers still described themselves as
defect: Three of four converted wrappers still described themselves as recording or emitting diagnostics, which the new return contract made false.
rule: After converting an effect to a returned value, rewrite every doc comment that describes the old effect, verb by verb.
catch_how: grep the converted functions' comments for record, emit and append after the change and read each hit against the new return.

quote: means nothing to a reader and restarts per file, giving two unrelated
defect: Locals numbered by a generator script (kept0, keptDiags1) meant nothing to a reader and restarted per file, so unrelated sites shared names.
rule: Never keep identifiers produced by a script's counter; name each local for what it holds before the change is pushed.
catch_how: grep the changed files for counter-shaped names such as a letter run followed by digits and reject each hit.

quote: One is ok instead: recordUnhomedKeywords already had a kept, the slice of
defect: Renaming a local to kept shadowed an existing kept slice in recordUnhomedKeywords; only the differing types let the compiler notice, and a same-typed collision would have changed the function's output silently.
rule: When renaming a local to a new name, grep the enclosing function for an existing binding of that name first; the compiler catches the collision only when the types differ.
catch_how: before each rename, grep the enclosing function body for the new name and reject any existing declaration of it.

quote: Splitting "a && b" into a preset variable and a later if was mine
defect: A compound condition was split into a precomputed variable and a later if, which changes when the operands are evaluated; nesting the original condition is what the code meant.
rule: When a compound condition is split into a precomputed variable and a later branch, confirm the operands are side-effect free and unchanged between the two points, or nest the original condition.
catch_how: compare the original and split forms' operand evaluation, including any state changed by the code between the two points.

quote: A fourth mutation reported "survived" against a pattern that did not exist
defect: A mutation run reported survived against a pattern that matched no line, so the file was never changed and the result proved nothing.
rule: A mutation that reports survived must first show the mutated file differs from the original; a pattern that matches nothing proves nothing.
catch_how: after each mutation, diff the file against HEAD and confirm changed lines before reading the test result.
covered_ref: Plant the defect and watch it go red.

quote: The as-landed notes for dynamicAnchors and diagnosedConstraints ended up
defect: Notes that corrected two table rows sat above the table and said see below while pointing up, so the cross-references ran the wrong way.
rule: Check cross-references such as 'see below' or 'above' against their final positions after the last edit, and confirm each one lands on the content it names.
catch_how: render the document and follow each cross-reference; each must reach the content it names.

quote: failed to correct the row
defect: #191 departed from a prescribed design item but left the design row prescribing the rejected approach, so the doc instructed what the code deliberately did not do.
rule: When a change departs from a prescribed design item, correct the design document in the same change; a reversal recorded only in code or a PR body leaves the doc prescribing the rejected approach.
catch_how: after each deviation from a design doc, grep the doc for the deviating item and confirm its row matches the code.
covered_ref: Sweep every site of the mechanism before closing it.

quote: I first measured the core with a regex over the source and reported 57 mutually
defect: The mutually recursive method count came from a line regex that ran each function to the next column-zero brace, which inflated the cycle from 27 to 57 and sized a plan on the wrong number.
rule: Measure code structure with a parser or the type checker, and cross-check the number with a second method before it drives a plan or a test.
catch_how: count the same set with go/ast and go/types and compare; a disagreement means the text-matching method is wrong.
covered_ref: Prefer proving a claim over asserting it

quote: The test claimed the schema walk was "the one mutual recursion the
defect: The archtest asserted only the largest mutual recursion and described it as the only one, so two smaller cycles went unchecked and a new cycle elsewhere would pass.
rule: A test that pins 'the only X' must enumerate every X it can find and fail on any unlisted member; asserting only the largest instance leaves the rest unchecked.
catch_how: plant a second, small cycle in an unrelated file and confirm the test names it.

quote: matching only the pointer form was invisible rather than wrong
defect: The recursion scan matched only pointer receivers, so a value-receiver method could join a cycle without the test noticing.
rule: When a discovery scan matches methods by receiver, match both the pointer and the value receiver forms.
catch_how: plant a value-receiver method that calls back into the cycle and confirm the scan reports it.

quote: the rationale soleAnchorSite had restated: ctx.go's diagAt already records
defect: Converted functions restated the diagnostic-return rationale that diagAt already documents, giving the same reasoning a second place to drift.
rule: State a design rationale once beside the mechanism it governs; converted functions should carry only the detail local to them.
catch_how: grep the package for the rationale's key phrase and expect one occurrence.
covered_ref: a second telling of the why never qualify

quote: a call-graph reading files it as a leaf
defect: A call-graph reading that counted only call expressions treated a method passed as a value as a leaf, so a dependency on the diagnostic recorder was missed.
rule: When analysing dependencies from a call graph, include method values and function references, not only call expressions.
catch_how: grep for selector expressions on the receiver type that are not followed by an open parenthesis and count them as edges.

quote: appendDiag forwarded one argument to l.diags.Append and its comment claimed
defect: A comment called appendDiag the single append point for lowering diagnostics, which stopped being true once lowerings began returning diagnostics to their callers.
rule: A comment that says a function is the only path for something ('the single', 'the only') must be re-verified by grep whenever a new caller or a return-based path is added.
catch_how: grep the callers and the return-based paths of the named operation and check the uniqueness claim against them.
