quote: the schemas block but not the `paths` key, and dropping the key reddened nothing anywhere in
defect: The original componentSpec test asserted the prefix and schemas but not the paths key, so dropping that key reddened nothing.
rule: A test of a fixture builder must assert every structural key the builder writes, since an unasserted key can be removed with no test reddening.
catch_how: Delete each key the builder writes, one at a time, and confirm a test fails for each.
covered_ref: Break what a test claims to catch.

quote: and `pass.Validate` with zero violations and zero diagnostics
defect: A document with an absent, empty, stale or nonsense irVersion passed irverify and pass.Validate cleanly, because nothing read the field.
rule: For every version or stamp field a document carries, have a verifier read it and reject absent or incompatible values; a field no check reads is invisible to every gate.
catch_how: Decode a valid document with the field removed, then with a bogus value, and confirm the verifier reports each.

quote: A worker that stopped partway through left zero values in its results, and the
defect: When a corpus worker stopped early, the comparison loop reported the unreached specs as 'compiled differently', sending the reader to look for a lowering corruption when nothing was compiled.
rule: When a comparison or check has more than one distinct failure cause (missing result versus differing result), give each cause its own branch and message; a failure message must name the cause that actually fired.
catch_how: Plant an early break in the worker (stop after N items) and read the failure text: it must say the items were never compiled, not that they differ.

quote: The Engine doc said the race property is pinned "only under -race" and left the
defect: The Engine doc comment said the concurrency property is pinned only under -race without saying whether CI runs -race, which was stale once main added -race to the coverage step.
rule: After merging main, re-read every doc comment that describes how a property is enforced (which test, which flag, which CI step) and check it against the gate as it now stands.
catch_how: grep doc comments for enforcement wording ('only under', 'pinned by', 'runs in CI') and compare each against the Makefile and CI workflow on the merged branch.

quote: A grep-based version of the same audit reported the same clean result and missed
defect: The first audit of the package-level-variable claim was grep-based and reported clean while missing both planted writes (index assignment and sentinel reassignment); the claim was only backed once an AST-based walk was used.
rule: Before trusting a clean result from a static audit, plant at least one violation of each write form the audit must catch (index, selector, dereference, reassignment) and confirm each is reported.
catch_how: Insert one planted write of every form (m[k]=v, x=nil for a sentinel, *p=v, s.f=v) into a scratch copy and confirm the audit reports each one exactly once.
covered_ref: Probe, don't read.

quote: The parameter-style completeness check counted deduplicated sets, so any
defect: The parameter-style completeness check counted deduplicated (name-set) entries rather than parameter occurrences, so a shadowed parameter could be deleted from both fixture and expectation without going red.
rule: A completeness check must count the same units the fixture is built from (occurrences, not deduplicated sets), and must be shown to redden when a single occurrence is deleted from both the fixture and its expectation.
catch_how: Add a second parameter that resolves identically to an existing one, delete one of the pair from the fixture and from the expectation, and confirm the check fails.
covered_ref: Break what a test claims to catch.

quote: The matrix reader ended the table at the first line not starting with a
defect: The table reader stopped at the first line that did not begin with a pipe, silently dropping that row and every row below it from every check.
rule: A parser for a structured document must fail loudly on a line it cannot place, never end the structure early and silently drop what follows.
catch_how: Insert a blank line and an indented row into the fixture table and assert the parsed row count equals the number of rows written.

quote: Six specs named capability rows their goldens do not show: a spec whose
defect: Six conformance specs claimed witness of matrix capability rows that their committed goldens do not actually exhibit, and one row (pagination) had only a false witness.
rule: Before a fixture is declared to witness a capability, read its golden for the construct that capability names; a witness label is a claim that must be checked against the output, not against the spec's subject.
catch_how: For each witness claim, grep the committed golden for the IR node or field the row names and fail if absent.
covered_ref: that claim is read by a reviewer, so weigh it like any other

quote: Two matrixRowsUncovered reasons pointed at an IR that could not hold the
defect: Two excuse reasons named an IR blocker that does not hold, although ir.LongRunning and ir.Idempotency already model those capabilities, so the stated reason was inaccurate.
rule: When a rationale names a blocker (a type, field or missing capability), grep for the named symbol and confirm it is actually absent before writing the reason.
catch_how: For each excuse string, grep the named IR type or field and confirm it fails to exist or fails to model the capability.

quote: OpenAPI cannot express is now rejected instead of living forever
defect: The uncovered-rows list accepted an excuse for a row that OpenAPI cannot express at all, so such an excuse could persist forever without any check objecting.
rule: An exemption list must be validated against the authority it excuses from: reject an exemption for an item the spec says cannot exist, rather than letting it sit silently.
catch_how: Add an excuse for a row the format marks absent and confirm the test fails.

quote: covers all nine format columns rather than one
defect: The legend-marker guard checked only one of the nine format columns, so a garbled marker in any other column went unnoticed.
rule: When a guard enforces an invariant over a family of columns or entries, iterate every member and plant a defect in a non-first member to confirm coverage.
catch_how: Garble a legend marker in each format column in turn and confirm the guard fails for each.
covered_ref: Sweep every site of the mechanism before closing it.

quote: parameter map is keyed on (name, location) as OpenAPI keys it
defect: The parameter map was keyed on the parameter name alone, so a legal same-name pair at different locations was silently collapsed to one entry.
rule: When choosing an identity key for a collection in a test or tool, copy the specification's own uniqueness key rather than the subset the current fixture happens to vary.
catch_how: Declare two parameters with the same name at different locations in a fixture and assert both survive the map.

quote: querystring parameter moves to its own path item, since 3.2 forbids it
defect: The fixture declared a querystring parameter in an operation or path item shared with an in: query parameter, which OpenAPI 3.2 forbids.
rule: Before writing a spec fixture, check the format's explicit prohibitions on co-location of parameters, not only its positive grammar.
catch_how: Validate each fixture against the format's prohibition list or a schema validator before committing it.

quote: Generating the expectation from the legal (in, style) table stopped the
defect: Deriving the expectation from the same pair table as the code let the table and the fixture shrink together, so a synchronized deletion still passed every check.
rule: An expectation derived from the same data as the code under test can shrink in step with it; anchor the count to an external authority such as the specification.
catch_how: Delete one legal pair from the table, its generated fixture rows, and regenerate the golden, then confirm a count check against the spec fails.
covered_ref: A corpus shares the blind spots of the code it covers

quote: fixture claiming its neighbour covers nothing the table covers, which was
defect: A fixture comment asserted that its neighbouring fixture covered nothing the table covers, which was not true of that neighbour's assertions.
rule: Before writing a comment that says another test or fixture covers or does not cover something, list that other test's assertions and check the claim against them.
catch_how: Enumerate the neighbour's assertions and compare them against the claimed coverage gap.

quote: Keying the reader on a leading pipe made it blind to a table GFM writes
defect: The table reader required a leading pipe, so a GFM table written without outer pipes escaped the single-table guard and every check in the file.
rule: When parsing a textual format, implement the specification's full grammar, including its optional spellings, rather than the spelling the project's own fixtures happen to use.
catch_how: Write a fixture table in every legal spelling (with and without outer pipes, last row included) and confirm it is found by the reader.

quote: Dropping the outer pipes from the table's *last* row removed it from the
defect: Dropping the outer pipes from the last row removed it from the contract while the row-count check still balanced, because the reader counted the line on neither side, so a golden update would have baked the drop in.
rule: A count check must take its expected value from an independent source (the raw text or delimiter structure), not from the same parser whose output it is checking.
catch_how: Move the last row of a table to a no-outer-pipe spelling and confirm the row count still differs from the raw-line count.

quote: Reading only \| as an escape
defect: The cell splitter treated a backslash-pipe as escaped even when the preceding backslash was itself escaped, merging two cells into one.
rule: When splitting on an escapable delimiter, handle the escape character's own escaping (a double backslash before a pipe) exactly as the format specifies.
catch_how: Feed a row containing a double backslash followed by a pipe and assert the cell count equals the visible cell count.

quote: A reason with no retirement condition is the same
defect: Three uncovered-row reasons deferred to a policy pass without saying what would retire them, so they read as closable gaps when they are not.
rule: Every deferral or exclusion note must state the concrete condition that retires it; a note with no exit condition describes a gap that looks closable.
catch_how: For each excuse or deferral string, check it names a retirement condition, and reject any that does not.

quote: instead of slicing a style
defect: The parameter-name builder sliced a style string that a neighbouring comment invited callers to pass empty, which could panic.
rule: A helper that indexes or slices its input must be total over every value its doc or neighbouring comment permits, or reject the invalid value explicitly.
catch_how: Call the helper with the empty input its neighbouring comment suggests and confirm it returns an error or a value instead of panicking.

quote: A fenced block was skipped only when the fence was written with
defect: The reader skipped fenced blocks only when they used backtick fences, so the same example written with tilde fences was read as a second table and failed four tests.
rule: When detecting a markdown construct, accept every spelling the specification gives it (CommonMark fences are backtick or tilde).
catch_how: Put the same fenced example in both backtick and tilde form in a fixture and confirm both are skipped.

quote: A line outside the table was reported whenever it held a pipe anywhere,
defect: The reader flagged any prose line containing a pipe character as a table row that fell out of the table, failing tests on ordinary sentences.
rule: A structural guard must key on the structure (cell count matching the header), not on the presence of one incidental character.
catch_how: Add a prose sentence that names the pipe character outside the table and confirm the guard stays silent.

quote: The pre-parse index was built through a package-level function variable so a
defect: A test seam was a package-level mutable function variable in a pipeline stage, which made the three tests that rebound it run sequentially and was a shared-state race hazard.
rule: Never use a package-level mutable variable as a test seam in a pipeline stage; carry the seam as an input option so each call sees only its own choice.
catch_how: Grep the stage package for package-level var declarations of function type and reject any that are reassigned in tests.
covered_ref: no mutable globals

quote: TestBuild_TracksAncestorsOnlyToItsDepthBound places its alias one level past
defect: The ancestor-depth test put its alias one level beyond the bound, so narrowing the comparison from inclusive to exclusive at the bound left the whole suite green.
rule: A boundary test must place a case exactly at the boundary as well as beyond it, and must be shown to redden when the comparison is narrowed by one.
catch_how: Change the bound comparison by one (for example < to <=) and confirm a test fails.
covered_ref: Break what a test claims to catch.

quote: Prerequisites of a single target are eligible to run concurrently under -j, so
defect: The gate target listed its checks as prerequisites, so make -j ran them concurrently, losing the CI order and letting fuzz write into testdata/ while coverage read the same tree.
rule: When a Makefile target's prerequisites must run in a fixed order or touch shared files, declare .NOTPARALLEL or chain them as one recipe, and check the target under make -j.
catch_how: Run the target with make -j and compare the executed step order against the CI workflow step order.

quote: The block introduced itself as the checks CI runs and listed nine commands, none
defect: The README build block still described a command list and a per-package coverage claim that the gate no longer ran, so the doc was false after the change that made it so.
rule: When a change makes a documented command list or claim untrue, grep every doc that repeats it and update all copies in the same change.
catch_how: grep the repo docs for each command or claim the change removes or alters and confirm no copy still states the old version.

quote: The header claimed the same commands and stopped there, which was the weaker
defect: The CI header said the workflow ran the same commands but omitted that the .NOTPARALLEL directive also keeps the order, so it stated only half of the guarantee.
rule: When a doc comment states a guarantee, name every condition the guarantee depends on, such as order as well as content, not just the first.
catch_how: List each mechanism that enforces the guarantee in the code and check the comment names all of them.

quote: The comment said two concurrent runs inflate the total several times over. That
defect: A script comment quantified the inflation from shared profile paths, a figure that stopped being true once the block merge landed in #381.
rule: When a change alters a mechanism that a comment quantifies, re-derive the number the comment states and rewrite it in the same change.
catch_how: Re-run the measurement the comment cites on the current tree and compare it to the number written in the comment.
covered_ref: Derive counts; never maintain them

quote: Both files said every check in the workflow runs a Makefile target. `lint` does
defect: Two docs claimed every workflow check runs a Makefile target, an overclaim since the lint step runs the golangci-lint action directly.
rule: Before writing that every member of a set does X, check each member and name the exceptions explicitly.
catch_how: Enumerate the set's members from the workflow file and check each one against the claim.

quote: FuzzCanonicalWords_Properties comes out of the quarantine. It was held back for
defect: A fuzz target stayed in the quarantine list after the issue that justified holding it was closed, so the target never ran.
rule: When an exclusion list ties each entry to an issue, re-check each entry's stated reason whenever its issue closes, and retire the entry in that change.
catch_how: For every quarantined entry, check whether the linked issue is still open and whether the target still fails without the exclusion.

quote: `BenchmarkAnchorWalk`'s fixture path was two directory
defect: A benchmark read a fixture path that did not exist, so it skipped silently with exit 0 and had never executed.
rule: A test or benchmark that can skip must fail when it skips in a gate run, or the gate must count executed cases and fail when that count is zero.
catch_how: Run the new target and count the reported results; a skip that still exits 0 should turn the target red.

quote: used a `chmod 0o000`
defect: A test skipped under euid 0 because root bypasses chmod, which left a statement uncovered and failed the coverage gate for root-run builds.
rule: Do not build a test fixture whose failure mode depends on the runner's privilege; choose one no user can bypass, and run the coverage gate as root as well.
catch_how: Run the coverage gate once as root and once as a normal user and compare the uncovered statements.

quote: A vendor extension declared on most OpenAPI objects reached the IR in no form at
defect: x-* extensions on most extension-bearing OpenAPI objects were dropped silently, and the tests had sampled only a few carriers so the gap went unseen.
rule: When a rule must hold for every instance of a construct, enumerate the instances from the source schema and assert each one, not a hand-picked sample.
catch_how: Derive the set of objects that admit the extension from the spec and assert each keeps the key in the IR.

quote: and nothing read it: two documents
defect: The encoding allowReserved field was accepted but never read, so two documents differing only in it compiled to byte-identical IR.
rule: For each source field a reader accepts, compile two inputs that differ only in that field and diff the IR; a field that changes nothing is being dropped.
catch_how: Compile a pair of specs differing only in the field and inspect the IR diff and the diagnostic list.
covered_ref: Compile the input; inspect the emitted IR

quote: `links` was preserved on a 2xx and dropped on
defect: The links map was kept for a 2xx response but dropped for a 4xx error response, though both lowerings read one source object.
rule: When two lowerings read the same source object, route both through one helper so a field added to one reaches the other.
catch_how: Put the same construct on each lowering site in one fixture and compare the IR entries for each.

quote: moving the read below the check left the whole suite green: every
defect: No fixture held an encoding that declared only allowReserved or x-*, so reordering the read below the empty-encoding check left every test green.
rule: When a fix depends on the order of a read and a later check, add a fixture whose only content reaches that path, and confirm reverting the order reddens it.
catch_how: Swap the two statements in the code, run the suite, and confirm a test fails.
covered_ref: Break what a test claims to catch.

quote: which ends every path the value walk produces
defect: Four assertion rows named the carrier as a bare .Unmodeled, which matches every map, so the placement check admitted any carrier in the document.
rule: An assertion that selects a target by path must fail when the selector matches more than one target, so check the selector's specificity as well as its success.
catch_how: Plant an entry in a wrong carrier and confirm the assertion reddens.
covered_ref: Break what a test claims to catch.

quote: ExtensionsUnder justified its keys only against unscoped ones, which does not
defect: A comment justified the distinctness of scoped keys only against unscoped keys, leaving out the non-extension keys written in the same scopes.
rule: A comment that justifies key distinctness must name the full key family the function writes, not only the family it was first checked against.
catch_how: List every key the function writes in each scope and check the comment covers each family.

quote: error branch they were being dropped on, and that x-* is simply preserved,
defect: The normative OpenAPI row still said x-* is simply preserved and links reach Response, statements the sweep showed untrue for most objects and the error branch.
rule: When a fix makes a normative doc row untrue, re-check every clause of that row, not only the clause the fix named.
catch_how: Read each clause of the changed row against the code path it describes after the fix.

quote: scope unescaped, so a name containing a separator read as two segments and two
defect: Form-part and callback names taken from the document were interpolated into a slash-delimited key scope unescaped, so a name containing a slash could collide with another object's key.
rule: When a key is built by joining document-supplied names with a separator, escape the separator inside each name through one shared function, and never interpolate a raw name.
catch_how: Compile two objects whose names differ only by an embedded separator and check their keys are distinct.

quote: The callback scope had it identically, so both now take
defect: The same unescaped-name key collision existed at the callback scope, a second site of the mechanism the form-part fix had already covered.
rule: Sweep every site of a key-building mechanism for the same escaping gap before closing the fix.
catch_how: grep for every interpolation of a document name into a key and check each site escapes it.
covered_ref: Sweep every site of the mechanism before closing it.

quote: carrierNarrows reported a carrier matching no
defect: The carrier-narrowing check reported a carrier matching no map as matching every map, so the check was wrong for its zero-match case.
rule: A predicate that counts matches must be tested on its zero-match and all-match cases separately, since a wrong sign in one can pass the other.
catch_how: Feed the helper a carrier that matches nothing and one that matches everything and check each result.

quote: and §12 gave a reason for the keys being distinct that was untrue
defect: The normative doc gave a reason for key distinctness that was false for two of the scopes and for pathItem, which no keyword spells.
rule: A rationale written for a set of keys must hold for each pair it names; check it against the least similar pair in the set.
catch_how: Pick the two keys most likely to collide and check whether the stated reason still separates them.

quote: The displaced keyword went nowhere else.
defect: When a bound's two keywords were co-declared, the displaced keyword was kept only in a diagnostic message, so {minimum:10,exclusiveMinimum:0} and {minimum:10} compiled to byte-identical documents.
rule: When one source field is resolved by dropping one of several co-declared keywords, keep the dropped keyword in Unmodeled and diff the IR for each variant pair.
catch_how: Compile the co-declared and single-keyword specs and diff the IR; identical output means the dropped keyword was lost.
covered_ref: Lossless by default, lowered late.

quote: The both-sides case added last round had each side lose its exclusive keyword,
defect: The both-sides test had both sides take the same arm of the reconciliation, so the other arm's write was never exercised in combination.
rule: For a test that covers both arms of a branch, choose inputs that reach each arm, and plant a mutation per arm to confirm each one reddens it.
catch_how: Instrument each arm, run the test, and confirm each arm is reached; then remove each arm's write in turn.
covered_ref: Break what a test claims to catch.

quote: minItems, maxItems and uniqueItems reached the IR in no form at all wherever
defect: The unhomed-keyword census left minItems, maxItems and uniqueItems outside its vocabulary, so wherever a position did not lower to a List (object, Tuple, hoisted scalar) those keywords vanished with no field, no Unmodeled entry and no diagnostic, while the census comment claimed the rest was captured.
rule: When a census or allow-list claims to cover a vocabulary, enumerate every keyword of that vocabulary and probe each one alone at every position that can carry it; a comment asserting the remainder is covered is a claim to test, not evidence.
catch_how: Generate one minimal schema per standard JSON Schema keyword, place it alone at each lowering position (component, property, parameter, allOf branch, scalar, object, array), and assert each keyword is kept in the IR, owned by a reader, or reported by a diagnostic.
covered_ref: Sweep every site of the mechanism before closing it.

quote: "valueConstraintKeywords excludes them for that reason" pointed at the
defect: A code comment's 'for that reason' cross-reference pointed at the sentence about ir.Tuple instead of the sentence stating that the bounds are List-owned, so the comment named the wrong justification.
rule: After writing a cross-reference inside a comment ('for that reason', 'see above', 'as noted'), check that the referent resolves to the sentence that actually states the cited fact, not a nearby one.
catch_how: Read each back-reference in the comment and follow it to its target sentence; confirm the target supplies the reason the reference names.

quote: the division is a claim rather than a proof repeated, verbatim, the sentence
defect: A comment paragraph repeated verbatim the sentence that the following paragraph already carried, so the same statement appeared twice in the census doc comment.
rule: Before adding a paragraph to a doc comment, search the comment for the sentence's wording and the adjacent paragraph's wording; a sentence stated twice in one comment is a defect to remove, not a reinforcement.
catch_how: Grep the comment block for each sentence's first six words after editing; any hit beyond the one intended line is a duplicate.

quote: the first row passed just as well when the boundary it names was reached and
defect: The cancellation table had a row for the first phase boundary that passed whether or not that boundary's ctx.Err check existed, because every boundary returned the same nil document, context.Canceled and empty diagnostics, and the left-counter assertion was zero on that row and so distinguished nothing.
rule: When a table of stop points returns identical observable output, give each row an observable that identifies which stop point fired (a call counter, a distinct sentinel) and assert it, so deleting any one check reddens its own row.
catch_how: Revert each stop-point check individually and confirm the row named for that point fails; a row that stays green under its own revert asserts nothing about that point.
covered_ref: Plant the defect and watch it go red.

quote: each went red, and all six were restored before the gate ran.
defect: The PR body reported that every cap and every ctx.Err check went red when reverted, but one ctx.Err boundary check did not redden at the time, so the stated verification result was an overclaim.
rule: Write a mutation or revert result into a PR body only after re-running the sweep against the final test files, and state the observed count per site rather than an expected 'all went red'.
catch_how: Revert each guarded site individually against the final branch state, record which tests fail per site, and compare that list to the sentence in the PR body before pushing.
covered_ref: Prefer proving a claim over asserting it

quote: streaming-media-31 witnesses more than it may claim. Its NDJSON request body
defect: The streaming-media-31 fixture witnessed the streaming-client row, which the matrix marks absent for OpenAPI, so the witness claimed more than the matrix allows.
rule: When a new conformance fixture is added to witness a matrix row, check the matrix status for that format of the row and of every other row the fixture exercises, and claim only the rows the matrix accepts.
catch_how: Run the conformance matrix test with the new fixture before pushing, and read each row the fixture names against its status for the format.
covered_ref: requires every expressible row to be witnessed or

quote: comment that called Grouping "one of the two" caller policies no longer counts
defect: A field comment kept a count of policies in prose ("one of the two") that went stale when a second policy parameter merged in from main.
rule: Never write a count of parameters, policies or options into a comment; name the members so that a later addition cannot make the comment wrong.
catch_how: After any merge that adds a parameter, grep the touched comments for number words and 'one of the' and read each against the current parameter list.
covered_ref: Derive counts; never maintain them.

quote: matrix still said OpenAPI reaches client streaming in no way at all, which the
defect: The ir-spec-matrix cell said OpenAPI reaches client streaming in no way, although the same PR made an NDJSON request body lower to streaming bidi.
rule: When a change makes a capability reachable, update the capability matrix row in the same commit that changes the behaviour, and rerun the matrix test in that commit.
catch_how: Lower a probe spec that exercises each capability the change touches, then compare the emitted streaming field with the matrix cell for that format.
covered_ref: requires every expressible row to be witnessed or

quote: The two now hold each other up. Reverting the cell and keeping the claim fails
defect: The commit says the cell and the witness cannot drift apart, but the claim is only checked for the absent-versus-witnessed pair, not for the warning-marked cell it says distinguishes an inferred stream from a declared one.
rule: Before writing that two artifacts cannot drift apart, mutate the one property the claim names (here the symbol, not just the presence) and confirm the test turns red; a claim the test cannot see is an overclaim.
catch_how: Change the warning-marked cell to the check-marked symbol in the matrix and run the conformance matrix test; if it stays green, the claim is an overclaim.

quote: classifyStream refused to name an element type whenever a direction had more
defect: The stream classifier refused to name the element type for any direction with more than one streaming content without comparing the contents, so a negotiated response whose contents shared one element type lost its Events.
rule: When a rule refuses on a count of candidates, compare the candidates first and refuse only when they disagree, and test a two-candidate case where they agree.
catch_how: Compile a fixture whose two streaming contents share one media-independent schema and assert the direction's Events is set.

quote: The diagnostic counted media types, which was wrong twice over: it fired for
defect: The several-streaming-contents diagnostic counted media types, so it fired for contents that agreed and counted one media type on two responses as several.
rule: For each diagnostic, write one fixture where it must fire and one where it must stay silent, and check that the unit it counts is the unit its message names.
catch_how: Compile the negotiated-shape fixture and assert the diagnostic list contains no entry for it; then compile a true disagreement and assert the entry names it.

quote: already used, so an operation reached by both heuristics now lists both rather than losing one.
defect: Provenance.Inferred was a single string that two heuristics could both set, so an operation reached by both silently kept only one of the two provenances.
rule: When two writers can set the same single-valued provenance or annotation field on one node, make the field hold both, or test a node that both writers reach.
catch_how: Build an operation that triggers both heuristics and assert that its provenance records both.

quote: The mechanism is not fully swept, and the rest is filed as #353.
defect: The PR closes #54 and #281 while four inline structural positions still derive hints two ways for the same reason that the PR fixes.
rule: Before closing an issue that names a mechanism, grep every site of the mechanism; if any site remains, fix it in the same PR or leave the issue open and say so.
catch_how: Grep the hint-deriving call sites across compilers/ and list each one against the fixed choke point; any site still outside it blocks a Closes line.
covered_ref: Sweep every site of the mechanism before closing it.

quote: handed the surviving branch the *enclosing* schema's hint,
defect: The {X, null} collapse gave the surviving branch the enclosing schema's hint, so two declaration orders of the same components produced different documents with no diagnostic.
rule: When a lowering hands a shared node to whichever declaration arrives first, derive the node's identity and every attribute, hint included, from the node's own location, and compare both declaration orders with hints included.
catch_how: Compile the same components in both declaration orders and diff the registries with Naming.Hint included; a single-order test passes on both orders of the bug.
covered_ref: Order-dependence needs a two-order diff.

quote: Their fixtures landed after this branch, so their
defect: Six goldens merged in from main carried hints that had never passed the naming grammar, so uppercase and path-character hints reached the committed corpus after the merge.
rule: After merging main, rerun the naming invariant over every golden in the merged tree, not only over the goldens this branch changed.
catch_how: Grep the merged testdata for hint fields containing uppercase letters or path characters and count the matches; any match means a derivation bypassed the choke point.

quote: The Components Object took no census. It was excluded as one of the maps
defect: The Components Object was excluded from the census as a map whose keys are all valid entries, but it is a fixed-field struct, so an undeclared key in it was dropped with no entry and no diagnostic.
rule: When excluding a type from a sweep, justify the exclusion from that type's own definition rather than from a neighbouring type's behaviour, and probe each excluded type with one undeclared key.
catch_how: Put one undeclared key on each object the sweep excludes and confirm that the IR or a diagnostic reports it.
covered_ref: Probe, don't read.

quote: the anchor; searching it raw found nothing, and a key with no node kept
defect: A key written as an alias was looked up by its raw node text, so the reader found nothing and the key was dropped silently.
rule: When a reader matches mapping keys in raw YAML nodes, match on the key the parser resolves, and probe it with a key spelled as an alias.
catch_how: Write a mapping whose key is an alias of an anchored scalar and assert the reader finds that entry and records it.

quote: A key holding a "/" spelled the scope of the object that path names, so a

quote: The duplicate message names the entry it repeats, as checkDuplicateIDs

rule: When a fix closes one position of an adjacency pattern, enumerate both orders of the pattern and probe each before closing the defect.
catch_how: Swap the operands of the mechanism in every rule that matches it and run a two-order or fixed-point probe on each.
covered_ref: Sweep every site of the mechanism before closing it.

quote: broke the property was the uppercase spelling one mutation away from it.
defect: The fuzz seed set held the lowercase neighbour of the input that broke idempotence but not the breaking input itself, so the property passed on the broken code.
rule: For a property or fuzz target, seed the exact input that breaks the property, since a passing neighbour one edit away proves nothing about it.
catch_how: Revert the fix and confirm the seed for the breaking input reddens the test.
covered_ref: Break what a test claims to catch.

quote: so a directive in a clean file is never read at all, and the
defect: golangci-lint's unknown-linter warning for //nolint directives only runs on files that have an issue, so a directive naming a nonexistent linter in a clean file passes the gate silently.
rule: Before relying on a linter's warning about a construct, plant the construct in a clean file and confirm the warning fires there, since many linters read a file only when it has findings.
catch_how: Plant //nolint:notarealinter in a file with no other findings and run the gate.
covered_ref: A check that runs is not a check that reaches.

quote: has never been in the enabled set here, so it never suppressed anything
defect: A //nolint directive naming a linter that was not enabled (forcetypeassert) suppressed nothing since it was written, and no linter reported it.
rule: For each //nolint in a change, confirm the named linter is in the enabled set, since a directive for a disabled linter is inert and no linter reports it.
catch_how: List the enabled linters from the linter tool and cross-check every //nolint name against them.

quote: The enabled set was asked of golangci-lint in whatever directory the caller
defect: The enabled-linter set was read from the caller's working directory while the directives were read from the repo root, so the verdict depended on where the script was run.
rule: A check that combines two reads of one tree must resolve both from the same root, never from the caller's working directory, and must be run from an unrelated directory to confirm it.
catch_how: Run the check from an unrelated directory and diff its verdict against the run from the repo.

quote: `jq -r '.Enabled[].name'` cannot iterate the null that golangci-lint emits when
defect: jq could not iterate a null list, and because jq reports only its last input's status the script exited 0 with the enabled set shrunk to the formatters.
rule: When a jq pipeline reads a value that may be null where an array is expected, default each array with // [] and check each jq call's exit status separately, since a combined call reports only the last input.
catch_how: Feed the tool a config with an empty linters list and check both the exit status and the parsed enabled set.

quote: Three of the four forms the check called blanket suppressions are not.
defect: The check classed //nolint:, a stray-comma directive and //nolint:allfoo as blanket suppressions, but only allfoo blankets; the others suppress nothing or only the named linters.
rule: When a verifier mirrors another tool's directive grammar, probe each form against the real tool and check its verdict per form rather than deriving it from reading the source.
catch_how: Plant each directive form in a file with a real finding and record which findings the tool still reports.
covered_ref: Probe, don't read.

quote: `scan` resumed two characters past each "//", which re-entered the same run of
defect: The scanner resumed two characters past each // so a run such as //// was read as two directives, double-reporting it and inflating the counts.
rule: When a scanner skips a delimiter, advance past the whole run of that delimiter rather than a fixed width, and test it with a run longer than the minimum.
catch_how: Plant a directive preceded by four slashes and check that it is counted once.

quote: `git grep -n` output, which folded the line number into the scanned text and
defect: git grep -n output was split on its first two colons, so a tracked path containing a colon was misparsed and its line number silently dropped.
rule: When splitting tool output on a delimiter, check whether the delimiter can occur in the data (paths may hold colons) and refuse or parse that case explicitly rather than misparsing it.
catch_how: Track a file whose name contains a colon and run the check against it.

quote: does not put it on PATH
defect: A CI comment asserted that the golangci-lint action does not expose its binary on PATH, which was false, and the step installed a second copy on the strength of that claim.
rule: Before writing a CI comment that asserts what an external action does to PATH or the environment, read the action's entrypoint or print the environment inside a job, since a local run cannot observe it.
catch_how: Add a CI step that prints which golangci-lint and the PATH entries before the claim is written down.
covered_ref: Probe, don't read.

quote: global commit.gpgsign with no key on the runner would fail the fixture commit
defect: The grammar fixtures inherited the caller's global git config, so a global commit-signing setting could fail fixture creation and make the suite read as a broken script.
rule: Fixtures that run git must isolate from the caller's global and system git config, for example with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, or they pass or fail by the machine they run on.
catch_how: Set commit.gpgsign=true in the global git config and run the fixture suite.

quote: The comment on the enabled-set sort claimed collation could fold two names into
defect: The comment justifying the C-locale sort said locale collation could merge shipped linter names, which it cannot; the justification was asserted rather than checked.
rule: A comment that justifies a defensive pin must name the input class it protects against, and that class must be checked on the real inputs rather than assumed.
catch_how: Run the sort under the default locale on every shipped name and compare the result with the byte-order sort.

quote: check_case bound the case name and never looked at it; the repo field is what
defect: The check_case helper took a case name it never read, a dead argument that nothing in the gate flagged.
rule: Remove any function parameter or local that is never read, since a shell helper's unused argument passes the gate unless a reader or a linter looks for it.
catch_how: grep each function body for each parameter name and delete any that never appears.

quote: The comment claimed the latter of both.
defect: A comment said that both the empty-name directive and the stray-comma directive suppress nothing, but only the bare empty form does.
rule: When a comment says which of several input forms has an effect, verify each form separately and state each result; do not generalise one form's behaviour to the group.
catch_how: Probe each directive form and compare each result against the comment's claim.

quote: go/scanner drops a trailing CR from a // comment before the nolint filter ever
defect: The grammar read nolint with a trailing carriage return on CRLF files, so it missed a bare //nolint that golangci-lint honours, an under-report.
rule: When a checker re-derives a tool's view of its input, list the normalisation the tool applies before its filter (CR stripping, BOM, trailing spaces) and add a fixture for each.
catch_how: Add a CRLF fixture with a bare directive and a mutation that removes the CR strip, then confirm the mutation reddens.

quote: Both were reachable and neither was tested; removing either now turns
defect: Two guard branches of the verifier had no test that reached them, so deleting either guard left the suite green.
rule: For every guard branch in a verifier, write a fixture or direct call that drives it, and confirm that removing the guard turns the suite red.
catch_how: Delete each guard in turn and confirm that some case reddens.
covered_ref: A check that runs is not a check that reaches.

quote: was missing the directive check as well as the grammar verifier;
defect: README.md listed the gate's command steps without the new nolint directive check, so the documentation no longer matched the gate.
rule: When a change adds a gate step, grep every document that lists the gate steps for a neighbouring step's name and add the new step beside it in the same change.
catch_how: grep -n the existing step's name across README.md and CLAUDE.md and confirm the new step appears wherever the existing one does.

quote: The walk's comment attributed the set to cycle termination and cited a
defect: The walk's doc comment credited the visited set to cycle termination and cited a two-schema cycle, which the depth cap already handles alone; the set is needed for branching (diamonds), not cycles.
rule: When a doc comment justifies a guard by naming an input, check that the named input actually needs the guard: remove the guard, run the cited input, and if it still terminates or passes, the citation is wrong and must name the case the guard is needed for.
catch_how: Delete the guard (visited set) and run the input the comment cites; if that input still terminates within the cap, the comment names the wrong case. Then run a branching input to find the real reason.

quote: fails quickly or says why — a walk that never returns surfaces as a
defect: The only test guarding the walk's visited set was a cyclic input that fails by package-wide timeout minutes later with no message, so a regression of the guard could not be diagnosed; no fast-failing branching case existed.
rule: When a guard's regression shows up only as a hang, add a bounded-time case whose input fails in seconds with a named cause (e.g. a branching shape that multiplies work) instead of relying solely on the input that hangs.
catch_how: Remove the guard and time the test package: if the only failure is a timeout with no assertion message, the guard has no fast, explained test. Add the shape that fails within seconds and confirm it reddens with a named assertion.

quote: The ancestor walk marked every schema it enqueued but not the one it
defect: The ancestor walk seeded its visited set with enqueued schemas but not the starting schema, so a composition cycle returned the start as its own ancestor and a schema whose mapping named itself answered to its own key.
rule: When a graph walk keeps a visited set, mark the start node visited before the first expansion; a cycle is the only way back to the start, so the start must be tested as well as the nodes it enqueues.
catch_how: Build a two-schema cycle where the start schema has a discriminator mapping naming itself (A allOf B, B allOf A) and assert the start's own discriminator value is empty; the revert of the seed must redden it.

quote: One neighbouring defect is left standing and filed as **#410**: a subtype named by *two*
defect: A subtype named by two mapping keys takes whichever key is declared first, so two documents differing only in key order lower differently; the defect predates the PR and was left standing with an issue.
rule: When a lookup yields a per-entity value from a collection that can name the entity more than once, compile the aliased spelling in both declaration orders before merging; if the order dependence is left standing, name it in the code and the PR body with its issue.
catch_how: Swap the order of two mapping keys that name the same subtype, compile both orders, and cmp.Diff the two documents; a non-empty diff means the lowering depends on declaration order.
covered_ref: A limitation that is deliberately out of scope must be stated in the code and in the PR body

quote: sourceindex landed while this branch was open, carrying its own copy of
defect: Merging main brought a fifth copy of the yaml-node builders (in sourceindex) into a PR whose title and body said the builders were defined once; a follow-up commit folded it in.
rule: After merging the base branch back into a refactor branch, re-run the sweep for the duplicated definitions the refactor claims to have removed, because merged-in code can reintroduce them.
catch_how: After every merge from main, re-run the grep for the moved definitions (e.g. grep -rn for the builder function names across the package tree) and require it to match nothing outside the new home.
covered_ref: Sweep every site of the mechanism before closing it.

quote: The third row is why an assertion was added. Dropping `paths: {}` from the fixture reddened
defect: A fixture element (paths: {}) could be removed without reddening any test, so the fixture's key assertion was vacuous until an explicit assertion on the preamble keys was added.
rule: For every element a test fixture declares, delete it and confirm some test reddens; an element the parser or compiler tolerates needs an explicit assertion.
catch_how: Mutate each fixture key in turn (delete it, one at a time) and run the suite; any deletion that leaves the suite green is an unasserted fixture element.
covered_ref: Plant the defect and watch it go red.

quote: package is instrumented only by its own test binary, so one with statements and no test
defect: A new internal package with statements but no test files contributed zero-count coverage blocks and would fail the 100% gate; it needed its own tests.
rule: Ship a new package with its own tests, because coverage is measured per package test binary unless -coverpkg is used.
catch_how: Run the coverage gate on the new package alone and inspect its profile for zero-count blocks before pushing.

quote: and the comment said electing it leaves nothing modelled behind. One shape
defect: A code comment claimed that electing content leaves nothing modelled behind, but one shape ({schema, content with no schema in the entry}) contradicts it; the claim was unpinned and inaccurate.
rule: Before writing a universal claim in a code comment, enumerate the input shapes the code accepts and run each through the compiler to check the claimed property; pin any counterexample in a test or narrow the claim.
catch_how: List the boundary shapes the comment's claim covers (e.g. entries with and without a schema), compile each, and check the claimed property (nothing modelled lost) on every one.
covered_ref: Prefer proving a claim over asserting it

quote: no committed fixture has an outside
defect: The hint-disagreement defect survived the whole conformance corpus because no committed fixture contained an outside $ref to an inline structural position.
rule: When a defect escaped the corpus, check whether any committed fixture contains the triggering input shape before closing; add a fixture that has it and confirm the fix reddens it.
catch_how: grep the committed corpus for the triggering construct (here an outside $ref to an inline position) before pushing; if none matches, add a fixture and revert the fix to confirm it reddens.
covered_ref: A corpus shares the blind spots of the code it covers

quote: depends on whether an unrelated schema points at the position
defect: For positions under /paths the hint depends on whether an unrelated schema references the position, so the same component set yields different names depending on content outside the position; deferred to #372.
rule: When two lowering paths can name the same node, check whether the chosen name depends on what else in the document references it, not only on declaration order; a two-order diff does not catch reference-dependent names.
catch_how: Compile the same position with and without an unrelated schema referencing it and diff the resulting names; any difference is a reference-dependent name.

quote: no longer excludes `ir.Naming.Hint` at all
defect: The order-invariance oracle excluded ir.Naming.Hint, which is the very field carrying the order-dependent hint bug, so the oracle could not detect the defect until the exclusion was removed.
rule: Do not exclude a field from an equality or order-invariance oracle unless the exclusion is justified by a probe; remove each exclusion and confirm the suite needs it before keeping it.
catch_how: Remove each exclusion from the diff helper one at a time and run the suite; an exclusion whose removal stays green is unjustified, and one whose removal reddens must name the field it hides.

quote: The recursion pin resolved a selector only when its base was the declaring
defect: The initial change made the recursion pin see method nodes but resolved a selector only when its base was the declaring method's own receiver, leaving free-function and parameter/local/field bases unread, so recursions through them were invisible.
rule: When a check claims to hold an invariant over call edges, enumerate every base-expression shape the parser can produce (receiver, parameter, local, field, returned value) and exercise each one, not only the shape the first case happens to use.
catch_how: Append one planted recursion per base shape to the tree and run the pin; any shape that leaves it green is an unheld site.
covered_ref: Sweep every site of the mechanism before closing it.

quote: A resolved selector is also looked for among the nodes of the package that resolved it, rather than in the graph's flat namespace.
defect: Resolved selectors were matched against the graph's flat, bare-name namespace, so a field read in one package could match a method declared by another package that uses the same type name.
rule: When a name resolves to a node, look it up in the namespace of the package that declared it, never in a flat table keyed by bare identifier, since two packages can declare the same name.
catch_how: Declare the same type name in two packages, with a method on one and a same-named field read on the other, and confirm the resolver does not cross-match.
covered_ref: a minted node needs a namespace of its own

quote: All three left the pin **green** before this change.
defect: The recursion pin stayed green on three planted recursions that leave through a free function and return through a method, so the pin's test did not test those shapes.
rule: Before trusting a regression pin for a construct, plant each shape of that construct into the tree and require the pin to go red; a pin that stays green on a planted case guards nothing for that shape.
catch_how: Plant a recursion per call shape in the tree, run the pin, and confirm red; then revert the plant.
covered_ref: Plant the defect and watch it go red.

quote: silence at the objects nested inside one: an example, an encoding, the
defect: An undeclared key was kept at objects that lower to a node with an Unmodeled map but silently dropped at objects nested inside those, such as example, encoding, oauth flows, and schema xml/discriminator/externalDocs.
rule: When a generic reader is wired to some object kinds, inject an undeclared key into every object kind the source can nest and assert it survives in the output; a reader wired only to the top-level carriers drops keys silently everywhere else.
catch_how: Generate one spec with an undeclared key on every nested object type and check each key's presence in the compiled Unmodeled maps and in the diagnostics.

quote: The components object was classified as a map with nothing to census.
defect: The components object was grouped with paths, responses and callbacks as a map with nothing to census, although its own key set is a fixed list of named fields that the census must read.
rule: Before grouping objects under one handler by shape, probe each with an unrecognised key to learn whether it is a fixed-field struct or a free-keyed map; shape alone misclassifies an object whose keys are a fixed list.
catch_how: Insert one unknown key into each object type the handler covers and check whether the key is reported, folded into the object, or dropped.

quote: entry says which object wrote it and two objects reaching one map cannot
defect: Entries written by several nested objects into one shared Unmodeled map were keyed without a source-path scope, so two objects writing the same key could collide and the surviving entry depended on lowering order.
rule: When several sub-objects write entries into one shared map, key each entry by its source path, and fixture two objects that write the same key so the surviving entry cannot depend on lowering order.
catch_how: Compile the document with the declaration order of the colliding objects swapped and diff the resulting map contents.
covered_ref: Order-dependence needs a two-order diff.

quote: The path-item census is deferred for two stated reasons. The second no
defect: A code comment deferring the path-item census cited a reason (httpMethods lacks query) that #293 had already made false, so the comment stated a stale justification.
rule: When a fix retires one reason a doc comment cites, re-check every remaining reason against the current tree, since the comment is only as current as its stalest clause.
catch_how: For each reason in the comment, run the probe it asserts against the current tree before the comment is merged.
covered_ref: If a claim about code must be written down, name the revision it was true at.

quote: methods against the library's nine. It has no `query`, the method OpenAPI 3.2
defect: The PR body still states that httpMethods has no query and that widening it would settle #293, which the later merge of #293 and the FU5 commit made false at merge time.
rule: After a later commit or merge changes a fact the PR body states, rewrite that claim against the final tree before merge; a body written before the last fix misleads the reviewer.
catch_how: At review time, grep each symbol or vocabulary the PR body names against the merged tree and fix any claim that no longer holds.
covered_ref: Review the **final** state, not an intermediate one.

quote: The quadratic is only half removed: scan.traverse follows every PointerPath with a PureRefTarget call on the same through-nodes
defect: PureRefTarget still scanned every pair of the wide mapping on each node PointerPath descended, so the reference scan stayed quadratic after the walk itself was indexed.
rule: When a fix removes a cost at one call site, grep for every sibling that walks the same nodes and measure the work there too before calling the cost removed.
catch_how: Instrument the pairs-read counter over a full compile of an N-component spec at two sizes and check whether the count still grows as N squared.
covered_ref: Sweep every site of the mechanism before closing it.

quote: Charging the index to cachedPairs halves the pair memo's capacity, and that memo is the anti-hang guard, not a speed feature.
defect: The key index was charged to the shared pair budget, so the memo that bounds merge-chain expansion held half the mappings it had before, turning an anti-hang bound into a speed budget.
rule: Before charging a new structure to an existing bound, state which guarantee the bound protects and measure how much capacity its existing consumer loses; never spend a hang guard on a speed structure.
catch_how: Feed fixed-width mappings through one view until the budget trips and count memoized mappings before and after the change.

quote: expand's memo hit (`if cached, ok := v.pairs[n]; ok { return cached, true }`, line 160) short-circuits the
defect: Because the index shrank which mappings stay memoized, a deep merge chain could stop expanding at all and emit an openapi/cycle-scan-failed warning that the same source did not produce before the change.
rule: When a cache decides whether a computation runs, a change to cache admission can change emitted diagnostics; diff the diagnostic list, not only the IR, across a cache-budget boundary.
catch_how: Read a chain deeper than the merge limit at a middle depth and then at depth zero with the cache near its cap, and diff the diagnostic list against main.

quote: One bound covering both is what keeps a second memo from doubling the memory the first one was capped at
defect: The doc says one shared count bound stops a second memo doubling memory, but index entries cost far more retained bytes than pairs (about 213 B against 76 B at width 1), so a 400x200 chain document retained 3.4 times the memory on this branch while the shared bound never engaged.
rule: A count bound documented as a memory bound must be checked in retained bytes, because different entry kinds cost different amounts; measure live heap after GC per charged unit before writing a memory figure.
catch_how: Measure heap in use after runtime.GC at the cap for the realistic shape and compare it with the figure the doc states.
covered_ref: Prefer proving a claim over asserting it

quote: keyIndex reasons only from the budget test and silently drops expand's other memoize gate, so the doc claim
defect: keyIndex repeated only the budget half of memoize's admission test and omitted the complete-or-entry-point condition, so its doc claim that it never holds an expansion the pairs do not was false whenever an expansion was in flight.
rule: When a derived cache is gated on another cache, gate it on that cache's own presence or result rather than a copied admission test, since a copy silently drops whichever conditions it omits.
catch_how: Force the source cache to decline an expansion (mark an input in flight) and assert the derived cache is also absent for that node.

quote: The index is a net pessimization at every mapping width the compiler actually sees
defect: The index was built for mappings under 16 pairs, 99.5 percent of the corpus builds, and most builds served zero or one read, so the map cost more than the scan it replaced for nearly every real mapping.
rule: Before shipping a cache, histogram build count and reads-per-build over the committed corpus at real widths; if the typical build serves fewer reads than it costs, gate it on width or reuse.
catch_how: Log width and read count for every index build across testdata and check the median reads-per-build before merging.

quote: builds a fresh View per call and reads each mapping at most twice, so the index is pure overhead there
defect: A change to a shared read path made declaresResourceIDAbove, which builds and discards a view per call, 1.34 to 1.50 times slower, and the PR listed that caller as an untouched adjacent finding.
rule: Benchmark every caller of a changed read path at its real access pattern, especially callers that build and discard state per call, before calling the change a win.
catch_how: Run the benchmark for each function that calls the changed one, not only the one the issue names, and compare ns/op and allocs/op against main.

quote: A zero-pair mapping charges nothing, so it is indexed unconditionally
defect: The budget test charged by pair count, so an empty mapping cost zero and every empty mapping was indexed after the budget was spent, leaving the key map growing with the document's node count; the test pinning the gate used only one-pair rows.
rule: A budget that charges per unit must also bound the zero-unit case: when an entry can cost zero, add a per-entry minimum or a separate count, or the cap never trips.
catch_how: Fill the budget to its cap, insert zero-cost entries in a loop, and assert the entry count stops growing.
covered_ref: Every loop, queue, retry, buffer, and timeout has an explicit limit

quote: This PR is #338's index, adds a second memo to that same shared view, and cites neither #404 nor #402
defect: The change added a second memo to the shared view that issue #404 asked to be settled first, and neither the code, the commit nor the PR body cites #404 or states a departure from its recorded decision.
rule: Before changing a shared cache or view, search the tracker for open issues about its consistency and either follow their recorded condition or state the departure in the code and the PR body.
catch_how: Run gh issue list with the file or type name as the search term and read any open issue that asks for an ordering or a settlement before the change.
covered_ref: Follow the recorded reasoning or say why you are departing from it

quote: Closes #338" retires an issue whose two largest items this PR deliberately declines
defect: The PR closed issue 338 while deliberately declining its two largest items, a per-node key map and a pointer-to-node map, and the measured reason for declining was recorded only in the PR body rather than beside the code that declines it.
rule: Use Refs rather than Closes when the change deliberately leaves part of an issue undone, and record the declined part and its measurement in the code beside the code that declines it.
catch_how: List the issue's checklist items and map each to a diff hunk or a written reason before writing the Closes line.
covered_ref: A limitation that is deliberately out of scope must be stated in the code and in the PR body

quote: The benchmark measures a shape no production caller has, covers no width below 64, and end-to-end the change is unmeasurable
defect: The benchmark added to justify the index measured a best-case shape no production caller uses, and a full compile of the spec class that motivated the change showed no measurable gain.
rule: Justify a performance change with an end-to-end measurement on the input class that motivated it; a microbenchmark of a best-case shape that no caller uses is an illustration, not evidence.
catch_how: Run full-compile benchmarks on the motivating spec at two sizes, before and after, recording time and allocation counts.

quote: Two of the three new subtests dereference a possibly-nil *yaml.Node inline
defect: Two new subtests dereferenced ChildByToken or RawChildNode results without a nil guard, so a regression in either reader would panic the test run instead of failing the assertion written to catch it.
rule: In a test, guard any pointer result with require.NotNil before reading its fields, so a regression fails with a message rather than panicking the package.
catch_how: Plant a mutation that makes the reader return nil for a present key and confirm the test fails with a message, not a panic.
covered_ref: preconditions, `assert` for values

quote: it reddens two. This subtest passes under that mutation.
defect: The PR body said routing RawChildNode through the view reddens all three cases of the raw-read test, but a repeated-key subtest passes under that mutation because both readers agree by design.
rule: Before claiming a test catches a mutation, run the mutation and read each subtest's result rather than the parent's; a subtest whose two readers agree by design cannot redden.
catch_how: Plant the named mutation and run the test with -v to see per-subtest pass or fail.
covered_ref: Plant the defect and watch it go red.

quote: TestChildByToken_IndexAgreesWithTheScanItReplaces never asserts the index was built, so a change that silently disables it leaves the test green
defect: The test meant to pin index-versus-scan agreement compared the scan against itself when the index was disabled, so the test stayed green with the index absent.
rule: For a test that checks a fast path against a reference, first assert the fast path was taken (its cache is populated), then compare results.
catch_how: Force the fast path off (return nil on entry) and run the test; it must fail.
covered_ref: Plant the defect and watch it go red.

quote: but no fixture is that shape and none can be
defect: The test doc claimed coverage of an alias standing in for a whole mapping and of mappings whose effective pairs differ from their literal pairs, but no fixture in the table constructs either shape.
rule: A test doc comment that lists the cases it covers must name a table row for each; check every named case against the table and correct the comment when a case has no row.
catch_how: Grep the table for each case the comment names; a missing row means the comment is wrong.
covered_ref: a doc comment that is imprecise

quote: New() eagerly allocates the keys map, so every View costs 37% more to construct
defect: New() allocated the key-index map for every view, including the views whose call sites never read through ChildByToken, adding bytes and an allocation to each.
rule: Allocate a map that most constructed values never write on first write, not in the constructor.
catch_how: Benchmark the escaping constructor with allocs/op before and after adding the field.

quote: mappingChild re-derives the pairs before consulting the index, so the hot path pays two pointer-keyed map lookups where one suffices
defect: The warm read path re-derived the pairs, a memo lookup, before checking the index, so an index hit paid two map lookups and, past the budget, re-expanded the mapping before falling back to the scan.
rule: On a cached-read path, check the cache first and return; derive the uncached value only on a miss.
catch_how: Benchmark warm reads with allocs/op for the cache-first ordering against the derive-first ordering.

quote: test asserted only the answer, which both readings give, so it now plants a divergence between index and pairs
defect: The PureRefTarget test asserted only the returned answer, which the index and the scan both produce, so it could not see the index being bypassed.
rule: A test for a fast path must show which path answered, by planting a disagreement between the two sources; an assertion on the result alone passes under both.
catch_how: Make the index and the scan disagree on purpose in a fixture and check which one the function returns.
covered_ref: Break what a test claims to catch.

quote: the index being reached, and nothing runs it in CI
defect: A benchmark comment said a flat per-component cost showed the index was reached, but no CI step ran the benchmark, so that claim was checked by nobody.
rule: A comment that says a measurement proves a property must name the job that runs it; if none runs, turn the property into a test that does.
catch_how: grep the CI workflow for the benchmark command; if it is absent, the comment's claim is unchecked.
covered_ref: A check that runs is not a check that reaches.

quote: NameFromDeclaration wrote the caller's hint straight onto the node, where
defect: NameFromDeclaration assigned the raw hint instead of the neutralized form interning writes, so a coordinate reached first by a reference held a different name from one reached first by its declaration, making the IR depend on declaration order.
rule: When a new path writes a field that an existing path derives through a normalizer, route the new path through the same normalizer, then prove agreement with a two-order diff.
catch_how: Compile a spec that declares a component and a reference to one of its inline positions in each order and cmp.Diff the two documents.
covered_ref: Order-dependence needs a two-order diff.

quote: a position whose node already exists resolves to it and returns **before** interning anything
defect: The first placement of the placeholder replacement, at intern, missed positions whose node already existed and returned before intern ran, so marking the alias alone left the naming bug in place while the test stayed green.
rule: When a fix hooks a construction path, enumerate every early return that bypasses the hook, and write a case reaching each with the node already present.
catch_how: For each early return before the hook, write a fixture that reaches it with the node pre-existing, then revert the fix and confirm that fixture turns red.

quote: lower to a node with an Unmodeled map of their own, and dropped in
defect: Undeclared keys on objects nested inside a node with an Unmodeled map (example, encoding, oauth flows, schema xml/discriminator/externalDocs, operation and tag externalDocs, components) were dropped in silence, despite the initial commit claiming x-* and undeclared keys were read at every object.

catch_how: Compile one spec that puts an undeclared key on every object kind in the grammar and diff the Unmodeled entries against the source keys; any missing entry is a site the sweep missed.
covered_ref: Sweep every site of the mechanism before closing it.

quote: applyPathItem runs once per operation an item produces, so an item that
defect: A path item that produces zero operations never reached applyPathItem, so its servers, extensions and undeclared keys were dropped whole with no diagnostic.
