catch_how: Build a spec with a path item that declares servers and an extension but no operation, then diff the IR's Unmodeled entries against the source keys.

quote: `provenance: svc.Provenance` is the document root, so every unmounted item's servers diagnostic is byte-identical
defect: The unmounted-item carrier stamped the document-root provenance on its servers notice, so N unmounted items produced identical diagnostics that compile.Diags deduplicated into one that names none of them, and its message claimed an operation the item does not have.
rule: A diagnostic about one of several similar sites must carry that site's own provenance, and it must differ from its siblings' diagnostics, so the dedupe on diagnostic identity cannot merge them.
catch_how: Compile a document with three similar items each carrying the same field and count the surviving diagnostics; the count must equal the number of items and each must name its item.
covered_ref: Compile the input; inspect the emitted IR *and* the full diagnostic list.

quote: Stale after the merge: `additionalOperations` is no longer dropped.
defect: A test-control comment still said additionalOperations is dropped and that the census treats it as a method-vocabulary case, after a merged PR (#310) made it lower as real operations.
rule: After merging main into a branch, re-check every comment and test justification whose stated reason depends on behaviour the merge changed, by re-running the probe it cites on the merged tree.
catch_how: After each merge, grep the branch's comments for the constructs they name and compile a minimal input for each claim to confirm it still holds.

quote: The callback route never reaches the unmounted-item carrier, so a callback path item that mounts no operation still loses everything in silence.
defect: The callback expression route lacked the mounted-zero branch, so an unmounted callback item lost its servers, extensions and undeclared keys with no entry and no diagnostic.
rule: When a new branch is added to one of several routes that lower the same construct, check every route reaches it, and compile an input for each route rather than trusting the route list.
catch_how: Compile one spec in which the same construct is placed under each route (path, webhook, callback) with no mounted operation and confirm each one produces a diagnostic and an Unmodeled entry.
covered_ref: Sweep every site of the mechanism before closing it.

quote: The warning asserts a preservation that did not happen: it is gated on what the *source model* wrote, not on what was actually kept.
defect: The announcement that servers, extensions and keys were kept was decided from the source model's view, which includes YAML merge keys the raw-node reader does not see, so the warning claimed a preservation that never happened.
rule: A diagnostic that claims something was kept must be decided from what was actually written to the output, not from a predicate over the input model, since the two readers can disagree.
catch_how: Compile a path item whose servers arrive through a YAML merge key and assert the keep-claim diagnostic appears only when the Unmodeled entry exists.

quote: `pathItemDeclaresAnything` omits `parameters` (and the docs pair), so an unmounted item that declared only those is dropped whole with no entry *and* no diagnostic
defect: The predicate deciding whether an unmounted item is announced omitted parameters, so an item whose only content was parameters was dropped silently, and a test pinned that silence as correct.
rule: When a predicate gates whether an entity is announced or kept, derive it from the writer's full field list, and probe an input where only each individual field is set to confirm none is silent.
catch_how: For each field the writer handles, build an unmounted item whose only content is that field and assert the output is non-empty or the diagnostic fires.

quote: `TestPathItem_WithNoOperationAndNothingToKeepIsSilent` (operations_test.go:2042) uses `/described: {summary: s, description: d}` as its fixture and asserts
defect: A test named for an input with nothing to keep used a fixture carrying summary and description and asserted the loss as correct, so the test pinned data loss rather than guarding against it.
rule: A test whose name claims an outcome must use an input that truly has nothing to keep, and a silence assertion must be backed by a probe showing the input's content is absent from the output.
catch_how: Compile the test's fixture and grep the output for each content field; if any content field appears in the Unmodeled map or is absent without a diagnostic, the assertion is pinning a loss.

quote: `go test ./compilers/openapi/... -count=1`: **every package green**
defect: The stated mutation that the test was said to catch was planted and no package went red, so the test's docstring and the PR body's bite claim were false.
rule: Before a test's docstring or the PR body cites a mutation as proof that the test bites, plant that exact mutation and confirm the cited test goes red.
catch_how: Swap the stated predicate for the stated alternative in a scratch edit, run go test on the package, and confirm the named test fails; if no test fails, the claim is false.
covered_ref: Plant the defect and watch it go red.

quote: A routine `go get -u` that adds one method to `standardHttpMethods` therefore deletes every operation written under it, with a clean `validate`, a clean `harness.Check` and green goldens.
defect: Two independent method vocabularies gated keeping an operation, so a method the library knows but the compiler does not lower was dropped silently instead of kept and announced.
rule: When two independently maintained vocabularies decide whether a construct is kept, bind the drop path to the one that keeps and announces, so an unknown member fails loudly rather than silently.
catch_how: Remove one method from the compiler's list in a scratch edit and confirm the operation still appears in Unmodeled with a warning; a silent drop means the lists are not bound.

quote: as they are dropped on a **mounted** item too (verified: neither survives anywhere today)
defect: The PR body and linked issue claimed a path item's summary and description are dropped on mounted items too, which the compiler does not do; the pair survives on every mounted operation.
rule: Before writing into a PR body or issue that a construct is absent or dropped everywhere, run the cited command on each route, including the mounted case, and quote the output.
catch_how: Run the exact grep the PR cites against a spec that mounts the same item; a nonzero count falsifies the claim that it is dropped everywhere.
covered_ref: Probe, don't read.

quote: The announcement is stamped at `declPtr` while the entries are keyed by `mountPtr`, so a `$ref`'d unmounted item mounted N times writes N key namespaces and announces once, at neither mount site.
defect: One diagnostic announced a $ref'd unmounted item reached at several mount sites, stamped at the declaration pointer, so it named none of the mounts whose entries it described.
rule: When one diagnostic announces an entity reached through several sites, its provenance must name the same key the entries were stored under, and a shared fragment mounted at two sites must produce a diagnostic for each mount.
catch_how: Reuse one $ref'd path item at two paths and check that each mount pointer appears in a diagnostic alongside its entries.

quote: the hole is a class of four, and `undeclaredKeys` reports all four as clean.
defect: The comment said only one object type needed the workaround, but the library's embedded-map short-circuit affects four core model types, all of which the census reported as clean.
rule: When a comment or fix describes a mechanism as affecting a single instance, enumerate every type that shares the mechanism and check each before accepting the single-instance framing.
catch_how: Grep the library for every type that embeds the same map kind and call the census on a document exercising each one.
covered_ref: Sweep every site of the mechanism before closing it.

quote: The key slice is unbounded and document-controlled: `MaxUnknownKeys` bounds what is *kept*, not what is allocated to decide it.
defect: The key list was built with no bound, so the document chose its size and the cap only trimmed what was retained after the full allocation, repeated once per operation.
rule: A cap on a collection must bound the allocation that builds it, not only what survives a later trim; size the buffer to the cap before filling it.
catch_how: Feed one path item far more undeclared keys than the cap and measure allocations against the uncapped count; they must not scale with the document's key count.
covered_ref: Every loop, queue, retry, buffer, and timeout has an explicit limit.

quote: Moving the sort out of `undeclaredKeys` makes it run on the calls that previously short-circuited
defect: Moving the sort above a function's early returns made it run on every no-op call, adding allocations across the whole compiler.
rule: When moving work across a function's early return, keep the guard before the work so the no-op path stays allocation-free, and measure allocations on a no-op case afterward.
catch_how: Run an allocation benchmark over the schema-walk hot path before and after the move and compare allocs/op on inputs with no keys.

quote: The path item's whole contribution is recomputed once per operation, producing N byte-identical results
defect: The path item's contribution was recomputed for each of its operations, so the census, raw-node scans and diagnostics were repeated N times and N-1 of the diagnostics were discarded by dedupe.
rule: When a routine runs once per child of a shared parent, hoist the parent-scoped work out of the loop, and measure allocations at one child and at many children to confirm the cost does not scale with the child count.
catch_how: Compile one path item with a fixed set of undeclared keys at one operation and at eight operations and compare allocations and surviving diagnostics.

quote: `pathItemDeclaresAnything` is a hand-maintained mirror of `applyPathItem`'s construct list, so the next construct added there silently loses its announcement.
defect: The announcement predicate restated the writer's construct list by hand, so any construct added to the writer but not to the predicate would be kept without being announced.
rule: Do not restate a writer's field list in a second predicate; derive the announcement from the writer's own result so the two cannot drift.
catch_how: Add a fake construct to the writer in a scratch edit and check whether an item carrying only that construct still produces a diagnostic.

quote: `len(diags) == 0 &&` at :608 cannot change the outcome.
defect: A guard conjunct was provably unable to change the outcome, so it was dead logic that reads as a live constraint.
rule: A guard conjunct that cannot change the outcome must be removed; prove it by mutating the conjunct and confirming no test or output moves.
catch_how: Replace the conjunct with true and with false in a scratch edit, run the package tests and the probe specs, and confirm the output is unchanged.

quote: pi is never nil: every caller of applyPathItem has already lowered an operation off it
defect: The nil precondition's stated reason was falsified by a caller added in the same diff, which calls applyPathItem with zero operations lowered, so the comment described a call graph that no longer exists.
rule: A precondition written into a doc comment must be re-checked against every call site in the same diff, including callers added in that diff.
catch_how: After writing a precondition, grep every caller of the function and check each one establishes it; a caller that does not invalidates the comment.

quote: No committed fixture reaches the new unmounted-path-item lowering, so it never meets the harness oracles.
defect: The new unmounted-item branch had no committed corpus spec, so the harness oracles (irverify, round-trip, determinism, order-invariance) never saw the Service.Unmodeled entries it writes.
rule: When a new lowering branch lands, add a committed spec that reaches it and confirm the oracle sweep sees the new output by grepping the corpus run for the new diagnostic or entry.
catch_how: Compile every committed testdata spec and grep the output for the new diagnostic's code; zero hits means the branch is unreached by the oracles.
covered_ref: A check that runs is not a check that reaches.

quote: Reword the message and all three go green while covering nothing
defect: Tests asserted the unmounted-item announcement by message substring, so rewording the message left them green and a duplicated or missing announcement at one site went unnoticed.
rule: Assert diagnostics by code, severity, count and pointer rather than by message substring, since a substring check passes for any rewording and cannot count per site.
catch_how: Reword the message in a scratch edit and rerun the tests; any test still green is matching on text, not on the diagnostic's identity.

quote: An anchor-valued undeclared key on a path item is invisible to the new census: it reaches the IR in no form, with no diagnostic.
defect: Keys derived from the library's folded map skipped anchor-valued pairs, which the unmarshaller short-circuits before the fold, so an anchored undeclared key was kept by nothing and announced nowhere.
rule: When a key set is derived from a library's folded or derived map, check the library's pre-fold short-circuits (anchors, merge keys) against the raw node, and prefer the raw node as the source of keys.
catch_how: Compile a path item with an anchored undeclared value next to a plain one and grep the IR for the anchored value's text; zero hits with no diagnostic is the defect.

quote: The carrier stamped the holding node's provenance, so an unmounted
defect: The carrier stamped the holding node's provenance on the unmounted item's notice, so two items produced one finding naming neither.
rule: A diagnostic about one of several similar sites must carry that site's own provenance, and it must differ from its siblings' diagnostics so dedupe on identity cannot merge them.
catch_how: Compile two unmounted items with different values and assert two distinct diagnostics each naming its own item pointer.

quote: The announcement was decided by what the source model reported rather
defect: The announcement was decided from what the source model reported rather than from what was kept, so a construct supplied through a merge key was announced as kept while nothing was.
rule: A diagnostic that claims something was kept must be decided from what was actually written to the output, not from a predicate over the input model.
catch_how: Compile a merge-key construct and confirm the keep-claim is absent unless the output's Unmodeled map holds the entry.

quote: All three routes that lower a path item
defect: The commit message for the path-item change claimed all three lowering routes reached the shared entry point, but the callback route did not, as a later review showed.
rule: Before writing that every route or site reaches a behaviour, enumerate each route in the code and probe each one, rather than asserting coverage from the route list.
catch_how: Compile the same construct under each route with no operation present and check that each route produces the expected entry or diagnostic.
covered_ref: Prefer proving a claim over asserting it.

quote: The merge of main moved the empty-list check behind unrecorded(), so
defect: Merging main moved the empty-list guard behind a call, so the sort ran on every no-op call and added three allocations per census.
rule: After resolving a merge conflict in a hot path, re-measure allocations on the merged tree, since a guard moved past a call silently reintroduces its cost.
catch_how: Run the allocation benchmark on the census path before the merge and after, and compare allocs/op for an input with no keys.

quote: the refusal's provenance on an overlay-grafted node reads `0:0` at the source's index
defect: The new openapi/tagged-mapping refusal reports position 0:0 under the source index when the tagged mapping was grafted by an overlay, so the diagnostic names no real location.
rule: A diagnostic added by a change must carry a correct provenance on every input path, including nodes an overlay or other transformation introduced; exercise the new diagnostic on a transformed node before pushing.
catch_how: Apply an overlay that grafts the offending node and assert the new diagnostic's source index and pointer, not only the source-declared case.

quote: `Load` was one line over the 70-line cap after the change; its tail — findings and resolution as diagnostics — is lifted into `findings` and `resolve`.
defect: The change pushed Load to 71 lines, over the 70-line function cap, and it had to be split before the PR could pass.
rule: After each edit, check the line count of every function touched against the 70-line cap and split it before pushing, rather than waiting for the linter to flag it.
catch_how: Run the function-size lint or make gate after the edit and read the line count of each touched function.
covered_ref: no function may exceed 70 lines or a cognitive complexity of 20

quote: `decode`'s doc comment claimed the decode is "the one place the yaml.v3 alias budget is spent, which is what bounds a billion-laughs expansion"
defect: The decode doc comment claimed the yaml.v3 alias budget was spent during the decode, which is false: decoding into a yaml.Node expands no aliases, so the guard never fires.
rule: Before a doc comment states what a dependency does at runtime, reproduce that behaviour once and check the claim against the measurement, not against memory of the library.
catch_how: Decode the fixture into the same target type the code uses and confirm the guard named in the comment actually fires.
covered_ref: Prefer proving a claim over asserting it

quote: drop omitted on the refusal path → survived until the refusal-path test was added, then red.
defect: The stream-drop report was missing on the refusal return path, and no test failed when it was removed until a refusal-path test was added.
rule: When a diagnostic must be reported on every return path of a function, add a test per return path that fails when that path's report is removed.
catch_how: Delete the report call on each return path in turn and confirm a test reddens for each.

quote: The premise is false and the defence it describes is backwards.
defect: The scan.Cycles doc comment claimed the yaml.v3 alias budget bounds expansion during the decode and that the alias weigher was a backstop; both claims are false.
rule: Before writing or keeping a doc comment that attributes a guard to a dependency, execute the claimed behaviour, and grep the repo for the same claim so every copy is corrected together.
catch_how: Run the fixture through the decoder the comment describes and check which guard fires; grep for the mechanism's name across .go and .md files.
covered_ref: Prefer proving a claim over asserting it

quote: That found four divergences, two of which no row covered
defect: Two of the four divergences between the parse reader and the byte-scan reader were in leading-document shapes that no hand-written readings-table row covered.
rule: When two readers of the same input must agree, compare them differentially over a generated space of shapes, not only over hand-written table rows.
catch_how: Generate leading-document variants (bare separators, nulls, anchors, tags, comments, directives) and diff the two readings for disagreement.

quote: a reused parse now has to carry the stream tail (a mutation dropping it silenced `openapi/stream-documents-dropped` with the whole suite green)
defect: The reused parse dropped the stream tail, so the stream-documents-dropped diagnostic disappeared on the path every CLI invocation takes, and no test failed.
rule: When an optimisation hands a cached result to a consumer, compare the cached path with the uncached path over the whole corpus, and confirm that some oracle actually takes the cached path.
catch_how: Run every corpus spec through both the fresh-parse and the reused-parse path and diff the diagnostics; drop one field from the cache and confirm a test fails.

quote: before, swapping `sameBytes` for content equality left that row passing.
defect: The equal-but-not-same bytes row could not tell reuse from a fresh read, so replacing the identity check with content equality still passed.
rule: A test meant to distinguish a reused value from a recomputed one must plant a difference only the reused value can show, and must be confirmed red under the weaker comparison.
catch_how: Swap the identity check for an equality check and confirm the row fails.

quote: one of which asserted `ErrParse` against a wrapper the pipeline no longer runs
defect: After decode was folded into decodeStream, a test still asserted ErrParse against a wrapper that no production path calls.
rule: When a refactor leaves a helper reachable only from tests, retarget its assertions to the entry point production calls, and delete the test-only path.
catch_how: Grep for callers of every function a test asserts through, outside _test.go files, and confirm each one is on the production path.

quote: I hit this exactly once while building it (past the cap, where nothing is parsed).
defect: A nil *Parsed was stored in the interface field, so a type assertion accepted it and the consumer would dereference nil on the path past the sniff cap.
rule: Never store a pointer that may be nil in an interface-typed field without a nil check at the store, and screen again at the reader; test both ends.
catch_how: Store a typed nil pointer in the field and call the consumer, asserting it takes the fallback path.

quote: A guard for this shape has to measure the walk, not its garbage.
defect: The existing cost guard asserted an allocation ratio, which a read-only quadratic walk leaves unchanged, so it could not detect the regression.
rule: A performance guard must measure the quantity the defect actually moves, and must be confirmed red on the reverted code before it is trusted.
catch_how: Revert the fix and confirm the guard fails; if it does not, change what it measures.

quote: The first version of this test was wrong and CI caught it.
defect: The first cost test timed sniff, which includes the parse, so it measured the parser instead of the walk and passed locally while failing on CI.
rule: A timing test must time only the function under test, with its inputs built outside the clock; confirm the timed region calls that function with a counter or probe.
catch_how: Instrument the function under test and assert the timed region invokes it once per iteration.

quote: so `sniff` took the byte-scan path and the "fixed" numbers I first measured were the scanner, not the walk at all.
defect: The benchmark input grew past the sniff size cap, which switched sniff to the byte-scan path, so the numbers measured a different function than the one under test.
rule: When a benchmark's input size is near a threshold that selects a different code path, pin the path in the test and assert it is the one being timed.
catch_how: Assert in the test which code path the chosen input size takes, and fail if it is not the intended one.

quote: Every reading in this compiler walks `Content` and treats an alias as a leaf
defect: An overlay graft produced an alias target outside every Content list, breaking the tree invariant all readers assumed, so a tagged mapping reached through the alias crashed the parser.
rule: When a transformation can build a node graph, list the structural invariant every reader assumes and check it on the output of every entry point that transformation runs through.
catch_how: After applying an overlay, walk the tree from the root by Content only and assert every alias target is reachable from it.

quote: a mutation that does not build looks exactly like one no test catches.
defect: A planted mutation that failed to compile was initially read as a result about the tests, so the mutation run gave a false signal until it was redone.
rule: Before reading a mutation run as a kill or a survivor, confirm the mutated package compiles and that the failure is a test failure rather than a build failure.
catch_how: Build each mutated package first and inspect the failure text of each red run.

quote: Two of these survived a first pass and are covered by tests added for them
defect: Two planted mutations survived the first test set, showing a branch of the new repair with no test that depended on it.
rule: Treat every surviving mutation as a missing test and add one before the PR opens; re-run the mutation set after the tests are added.
catch_how: Plant each mutation of the new branch and confirm at least one test reddens for each.

quote: The source has been refused for both shapes since #12 and #27.
defect: The overlay document reached the library without the cycle and alias-amplification refusals the source already had, so an overlay alone could crash or exhaust memory.
rule: When a guard protects one input entry point, list every other entry point into the same consumer (overlays, copies, grafts) and apply the guard to each before shipping.
catch_how: Feed each entry point the same hostile shapes the guarded one refuses and assert each is refused.

quote: The last survived a first pass and is why `applyOverlay` takes its findings as data.
defect: Dropping a forwarded warning in the overlay path survived mutation until a test asserted that the warning reached the caller.
rule: Treat every surviving mutation as a missing test and add one before the PR opens; re-run the mutation set after the tests are added.
catch_how: Remove each forwarding call in turn and confirm a test asserts the forwarded finding reaches the caller.

quote: Two survived a first pass and are covered by the `load` tests added for them
defect: Two planted mutations of the new budget and warning logic survived the first test set, so the load path had no test pinning them.
rule: Treat every surviving mutation as a missing test and add one before the PR opens; re-run the mutation set after the tests are added.
catch_how: Plant each mutation of the new budget and reporting logic and confirm at least one test reddens for each.

quote: The test took the minimum over every walk of the 16000-key tree, then the minimum over every walk of the 8000-key tree.
defect: The ratio test timed the two sizes in sequence, so a burst of background load landing on one size's runs alone pushed the ratio past its allowance and failed CI.
rule: A ratio assertion over two timings must interleave the two measurements so both see the same load; never time one size to completion before measuring the other.
catch_how: Run the timing test under synthetic background load with parallel packages and record the spread of the ratio.

quote: The doc comment used to say millisecond readings gave scheduling noise "no leverage" on the ratio.
defect: The test's doc comment asserted that millisecond readings made scheduling noise irrelevant to the ratio, a claim a CI failure disproved.
rule: Do not write a doc comment asserting a timing measurement is immune to noise; state the measured spread under load, or drop the claim.
catch_how: Run the timing under load and record the observed maximum ratio before writing any claim about it.
covered_ref: Prefer proving a claim over asserting it

quote: Without that assertion the test passed with detection ignoring the budget; with it, that mutation fails the test
defect: The engine's budget-refusal test passed with detection ignoring the byte budget until an assertion on the reported format was added.
rule: For each new refusal path, plant a mutation that skips the check and confirm the test that claims to cover it turns red; a test that stays green with the check removed covers nothing.
catch_how: Remove the budget check from detection and run the engine test; it must fail, not pass.
covered_ref: Break what a test claims to catch.

quote: A row declaring nothing can no longer pass on bytes that never parsed.
defect: Corpus rows that declared no key could pass on bytes that never parsed, so the table asserted nothing about those inputs.
rule: A table row must assert its precondition (for example that the input parses) before asserting the outcome, so a row cannot pass on input that never reached the code under test.
catch_how: Make a row's fixture unparseable and confirm the row fails rather than passing on the declined outcome.
covered_ref: A negative fixture must be reachable.

quote: That fixes the earlier attempt's other flaw, where the parse error was discarded and three rows made `Detect` emit diagnostics nobody asserted.
defect: An earlier attempt discarded the parse error in its corpus test and let three rows emit detection diagnostics that no assertion checked.
rule: Do not discard the error from a call a test depends on; propagate or assert it, and assert every diagnostic the call under test returns.
catch_how: Grep the test for discarded errors (`_ =`, `, _ :=`) and for returned diagnostics that are never compared.
covered_ref: Handle every error (`_ = err` is banned)

quote: A prose file with a line starting `openapi:` that fails to parse is claimed as a broken spec.
defect: Deleting the byte scan exposed that a prose file with a failing-to-parse openapi: line is claimed as a broken spec at every size, a defect the scan had hidden above 64 KiB.
rule: When deleting a path that declined some inputs, re-probe each input that path handled through the replacement at sizes on both sides of the old threshold, so a defect it hid is found before merge.
catch_how: Feed the old path's rejected inputs (prose with a key-like line, unparseable documents) to the new path at sizes above and below the old cutoff and compare outcomes.

quote: Its unparseable row had routed to "unrecognized" under the new rule, which would have silently dropped that path from the test.
defect: After the classifier change, a test row meant to reach the unreadable-source report routed to the unrecognized branch, which would have left that report path untested without failing.
rule: After changing a classification rule, check that each test fixture still lands on the branch its test asserts, and that the test fails if that branch is removed.
catch_how: Assert which diagnostic or branch each fixture reaches, then re-run the classifier-change suite and confirm each row still hits its named path.
covered_ref: A negative fixture must be reachable.

quote: Without the bound, a crafted 8 MB file of nothing but `openapi: prose` lines, broken at the end, spent 760 ms in the check after a 273 ms parse.
defect: The new per-line parse in the broken-source guard had no limit, so a crafted file made the guard cost nearly three times the parse of the file.
rule: Any loop that re-parses or rescans each matching line of untrusted input must carry an explicit cap, and the PR must time an adversarial input that maximises the matches.
catch_how: Generate a file of many repeated matching lines, broken at the end, and time the guard against the parse before opening the PR.
covered_ref: Every loop, queue, retry, buffer, and timeout has an explicit limit.

quote: On `main`, each of these compiles clean, exits 0, and loses the anchored entry:
defect: The bundled parser silently dropped anchored mapping entries at five models, so compiles exited 0 while losing paths, operations, responses, callbacks and a security requirement.
rule: When a dependency can drop input without error, compile a twin input that differs only in the construct and diff the outputs for missing entries; a clean exit proves nothing.
catch_how: Compile the anchored input and its anchor-blanked twin and cmp.Diff the two IR documents.
covered_ref: Probe, don't read.

quote: The last row isn't in #459. I found it by listing every core model that embeds a `sequencedmap.Map`, rather than trusting the four sites the issue named.
defect: The issue listed four sites of the anchored-entry skip; a fifth, the security requirement, was missing from the list and would have stayed broken if the fix had followed the issue.
rule: When an issue enumerates the sites of a defect, enumerate them by searching the code for the mechanism before scoping the fix to the list.
catch_how: grep for every type that embeds the mechanism's container (for example sequencedmap.Map) and run the repro against each one.
covered_ref: Sweep every site of the mechanism before closing it.

quote: Its tree never passes through `Load`, so an anchored entry there is still skipped in silence.
defect: The anchor fix covers only the root document; anchored entries in externally referenced documents are still silently dropped, deferred to a follow-up issue.
rule: When a fix covers one input route, enumerate every other route into the same code (external references, overlays) and either fix each or state the uncovered route where its reader will see it.
catch_how: Run the defect's repro through each input route the loader accepts, not only the root document, and compare outputs.
covered_ref: Sweep every site of the mechanism before closing it.

quote: My first draft broke that rule, and the self-test flagged it as a mutant broken outright.
defect: The first draft of the fuzz-retry self-test used anchors that broke the script it edits, so its planted mutants were broken outright rather than testing the retry decision.
rule: Before counting a planted mutation as caught, confirm it applies exactly once and changes only the intended site; a mutant that breaks the file turns the suite red for the wrong reason.
catch_how: Count the matches of each planted anchor and diff each mutant against the original; a mutant touching more than its target site is broken.

quote: Its raw output failed `golangci-lint` and left some ragged formatting, so this also:
defect: The automated go fix rewrite left code that failed golangci-lint, including redundant f := f loop copies and ragged formatting.
rule: Run the full lint and gofmt on the output of any automated rewriter before commit, and read each rewritten loop for copies the rewriter adds that the language no longer needs.
catch_how: Run golangci-lint run and gofmt -l on the rewritten tree before commit.
covered_ref: Before claiming any Go work done, run and pass the gate

quote: Entries now decode in ID order, so a document with several bad types reports the same one on every run.
defect: Type registry entries were decoded in an order that let a document with several invalid types report a different error on different runs.
rule: When decoding a map-keyed collection, decode in sorted key order so the first reported error is the same on every run.
catch_how: Decode a document with two invalid entries many times and compare the reported error across runs.

quote: The option types in `engine` and `compilers/openapi` follow the same tag rule, but nothing encodes them today, so no test observes those tags.
defect: The struct-tag rule is checked only for structs reachable from a Document, so the option types it governs go unchecked.
rule: When a convention is stated for a whole codebase, hold it with a test over every type it governs, not only the types one entry point reaches.
catch_how: Flip one tag on an option type and confirm a test goes red; if none does, the convention is unenforced there.

quote: (`FormatNilSliceAsNull` has no observable case, since no IR type holds a nil slice the encoder reaches, and it says so in the test)
defect: One option the canonical encoder pins has no fixture that fails when it is flipped, so its planted mutation cannot be observed.
rule: For each option a canonical encoder pins, confirm a fixture makes it observable; if none can, drop the pin or record why in the code, not only in the test.
catch_how: Flip each pinned option in turn and run the suite; any option whose flip leaves the suite green is unpinned.

quote: #507: `irverify` passes a string that is not UTF-8, which the encoder now refuses.
defect: The invariant checker accepts strings the new encoder refuses, so the verifier and the writer disagree about validity.
rule: When a writer starts refusing an input, mirror the refusal in every checker that claims to accept what the writer writes, in the same change.
catch_how: Feed each input the encoder refuses to the verifier and assert it reports a violation.

quote: Names read off a pointer's last token were taken raw: still RFC 6901-escaped and, from a `$ref`, still percent-encoded.
defect: Names read from a pointer's last token were used without unescaping, so a schema named Cat/Dog got discriminatorValue Cat~1Dog on the wire.
rule: Decode a structured identifier's token where it is extracted, and test a name containing each escape character through every consumer (wire value, hint, variant name).
catch_how: Compile a schema whose name contains '/' and '%' and inspect every name derived from its pointer or $ref.

quote: #517: an inline allOf subtype takes a pointer token as its implicit `discriminatorValue`.
defect: An inline allOf subtype takes a raw pointer token as its implicit discriminatorValue.
rule: A value derived from a pointer token must be checked for every position kind that produces a pointer (inline, $ref, allOf branch), not only the common one.
catch_how: Enumerate each pointer-producing position kind and assert the derived discriminator value in each.

quote: #518: a key spelled like a structural keyword skews the pointer-derived hint.
defect: A schema key spelled like a structural keyword changes the hint derived from its pointer.
rule: Hints derived from pointer tokens must treat every token as data: test a key equal to each structural keyword.
catch_how: Compare the hint for a schema keyed like a structural keyword with the hint for a same-shaped schema under another key.

quote: #519: an outside `$ref` names a pure-`$ref` position by declaration order.
defect: An outside $ref names a pure-$ref position according to which declaration the compiler meets first.
rule: A naming rule must give the same name for two declaration orders; compile both orders and diff the IR for every construct reachable by two routes.
catch_how: Compile the fixture with the two declaration orders swapped and cmp.Diff the IR documents.
covered_ref: Order-dependence needs a two-order diff.

quote: #520: a percent-encoded non-UTF-8 byte in a `$ref` fragment reaches an IR identifier.
defect: Percent-decoding a $ref fragment can produce non-UTF-8 bytes that reach an IR identifier, bypassing the UTF-8 check the raw source passes.
rule: After any percent or escape decoding of untrusted text, re-apply the validity check the raw input passed before the decoded text becomes an identifier.
catch_how: Compile a $ref whose fragment percent-encodes an invalid UTF-8 byte and assert the IR is valid and no invalid identifier is produced.

quote: #521: a `$ref` to an inline position names its union variant after a pointer token.
defect: A $ref to an inline position names its union variant after a raw pointer token.
rule: Name derivation from a $ref must branch on whether the target is inline or a component, and each branch needs its own test.
catch_how: Build a union variant through a $ref to an inline schema and assert the variant name is not a pointer token.

quote: #522: an extension an overlay adds is attributed to the base document.
defect: Provenance for an extension added by an overlay records the base document rather than the overlay.
rule: Provenance must name the document that introduced each node; for every merge layer, check the recorded source of each node the layer adds.
catch_how: Apply an overlay that adds an extension and inspect the provenance recorded for that node.

quote: #523: the cycle scan follows a `$ref` fragment that is not a pointer.
defect: The cycle scan follows $ref fragments that are not JSON Pointers, which the resolver would refuse.
rule: A reference resolver's acceptance rule must be applied by every walker that follows references, not only by the resolver.
catch_how: Feed a $ref fragment without a leading '/' to the cycle scan and assert it is not followed.

quote: `AppendToken` rewrites a byte that is not UTF-8 to U+FFFD, which could give two keys one pointer.
defect: A lossy rewrite of non-UTF-8 bytes could map two distinct keys to one pointer and so one ID; safety depended on an upstream refusal that had to be pinned.
rule: When a lossy conversion could merge two inputs into one ID, either make it injective or pin the upstream guard that keeps its input out, with a test for each input format.
catch_how: Feed two keys differing only in a non-UTF-8 byte through each source format and assert distinct IDs or a refusal.

quote: Before that case existed, nothing in the module failed.
defect: A refactored branch for dotless names had no test; a mutation changing that branch passed the whole module until a bare-keyword case was added.
rule: Before refactoring a function, confirm each edge-case branch has a test that fails when that branch's behaviour changes, by planting a mutation at each branch first.
catch_how: Plant a mutation at each branch (for example ok || true) and run go test; a mutation that stays green marks an unpinned branch.

quote: "Generally available" became "built by default".
defect: The emitter design said Go 1.27's encoding/json/v2 was generally available; the toolchain still gates those packages behind goexperiment.jsonv2, so the doc overclaimed.
rule: Before writing that a Go package or feature is stable or default, check its build constraints in the toolchain source rather than trusting release notes.
catch_how: grep the standard library package for //go:build goexperiment tags and check whether the default baseline enables them.
covered_ref: Prefer proving a claim over asserting it.

quote: "They stream" was narrowed.** Marshaling streams.
defect: The emitter design claimed decoding streams, but tag dispatch buffers one value because the tag can come last in its object.
rule: A doc claim that a path streams must be checked against any buffering in that path, and the buffering stated where it matters.
catch_how: Decode a large object whose tag comes last and measure how much input is buffered before the first value is dispatched.
covered_ref: Prefer proving a claim over asserting it.

quote: "Six IR constructs" said six where there are seven subsections.
defect: The section 8 intro gave a count of IR constructs that did not match the seven subsections it introduces.
rule: Do not write a count of documented items in prose; derive it from the list or omit it.
catch_how: Count the subsection headings under the section and compare with the number in its intro sentence.
covered_ref: Derive counts; never maintain them.

quote: The issue suggested `name, _ :=`, but `ComponentSchemaName` returns a non-empty name with `ok == false` for a top-level entry of another kind
defect: The issue's suggested fallback discarded ComponentSchemaName's ok flag, so a top-level non-component pointer would have produced a tag that no component answers to.
rule: When a lookup returns a value together with an ok flag, read and check the flag; a non-empty value with ok false is a valid return, not a found result.
catch_how: Place a subtype at a top-level non-component key (e.g. components/x-shared/Cat) and assert the lookup yields no name.

quote: Today it returns before the fallback, because it finds no discriminated ancestor (#572), so a mutation dropping the check stays green.
defect: The guard that rejects non-component names before the fallback was unreachable by any test, so deleting it left the suite green.
rule: For every guard added, delete it and confirm a test goes red; if no fixture can reach the guard, record the gap beside the guard and file it instead of presenting it as tested.
catch_how: Delete the guard and run the suite; if it stays green, the guard has no test that reaches it.
covered_ref: Break what a test claims to catch.

quote: a mapping entry that names an inline subtype resolves only when the subtype's enclosing schema lowers before the base
defect: Mapping-by-reference resolution depends on lowering order, and the test declares fixtures in one order to dodge it.
rule: When a test declares fixtures in a particular order to avoid a bug, file that bug and cite it in the test, because that order hides the defect from a two-order oracle.
catch_how: Swap the fixture's declaration order and diff the IR; grep tests for order-sensitive comments.
covered_ref: Order-dependence needs a two-order diff.

quote: #572: a subtype declared under an extension gets no `discriminatorValue`, even from a mapping entry that names it.
defect: A subtype declared under an x- extension silently receives no discriminator value, even when a mapping entry names it.
rule: When a lookup walks ancestors to find a declaration's context, test the subject under every container an OpenAPI document can place it in, including x- extensions.
catch_how: Declare the subject under each container kind (components, paths, x-*) and assert its discriminator value.

quote: The Install section said "Requires Go 1.26 or newer".
defect: The README restated the Go toolchain version as a literal, and it had drifted from the go directive in go.mod.
rule: Do not restate a version, count or name in prose when a single definition exists; point at the definition.
catch_how: grep the docs for every version literal and compare each against go.mod.
covered_ref: Derive counts; never maintain them.

quote: a child that returned straight after its `go` statement passed now and then
defect: The reach test for the goroutine check passed intermittently, because a planted goroutine could still be runnable when the check ran.
rule: Before committing a re-executing or timing-dependent test, loop it hundreds of times and record the failure rate; a test that sometimes passes when it should fail is not a reach test.
catch_how: Run the reach test in a loop of 1000 with and without the synchronisation (handshake, GOMAXPROCS=1) and compare failure counts.

quote: a rule keyed only on `ast.GoStmt` would have left one of the four packages outside its own guard
defect: A guard keyed on the go statement alone would have missed engine, which starts its goroutines through sync.WaitGroup.Go.
rule: Before writing a syntactic guard for an operation, enumerate every spelling the codebase uses for it (statement, method call, helper) and key the guard on all of them.
catch_how: grep the repo for each candidate spelling and check that every package the guard must cover is matched by at least one.

quote: Each fails to encode and verifies with zero violations.
defect: irverify accepted six kinds of ill-formed-UTF-8 string carriers that the Document encoder refuses, so a verified document could still fail to encode.
rule: A verifier must mirror each refusal its encoder makes: enumerate the encoder's failure cases, give each a verifier check, and in tests encode every document that verifies clean.
catch_how: Plant an ill-formed string in each string-bearing field, run verify, then encode; any encode failure with zero verify findings is a gap.

quote: Keeping them would report every such string twice.
defect: Two narrower UTF-8 codes reported the same ill-formed string that the generalised check also reports, so each defect would produce two findings.
rule: When a generalised check subsumes narrower checks, retire the narrower codes in the same change and assert that each planted defect yields exactly one finding.
catch_how: Plant one defect per carrier and count findings per defect in a test.

quote: Declared before its target, it has nothing to reuse and lowers to `any`.
defect: A schema reference declared before its target lowers to any when the resolver refuses the pointer, so its result depends on declaration order.
rule: When a compiler reuses interned results instead of asking the resolver, the outcome can depend on declaration order; run both orders of each reference pair.
catch_how: Swap the declaration order of each reference pair and diff the resulting IR.
covered_ref: Order-dependence needs a two-order diff.

quote: The issue also notes that the resolver's `unresolved-ref` is reported at the document root.
defect: Resolver failures on references are located at the document root rather than at the $ref that failed.
rule: Every diagnostic about a reference must carry the reference's own location; a root location is a defect to file before any test pins it.
catch_how: For each unresolved-ref finding, assert its location equals the $ref pointer.

quote: The pre-lowering cycle scan then walked it from the document root as a key and refused this document as a cycle
defect: nodeview read the fragment #x-s as the pointer x-s, so the cycle scan refused a valid document as a cycle.
rule: When two readers parse the same syntax, test both against one table of inputs and a differential fuzz target; one reader alone drifts unseen.
catch_how: Run a differential fuzz over reference fragments through both readers and report any disagreement.

quote: `#/components/schemas/%FF` became a pointer holding the byte 0xFF
defect: A percent-decoded fragment was used as a JSON Pointer without a UTF-8 check, so the IR held an identifier it could not encode.
rule: After percent-decoding or unescaping a value, validate it against the target format's own grammar (UTF-8 for a JSON Pointer) before using it as a key.
catch_how: Feed every percent-escape of a non-UTF-8 byte into each reader and encode the resulting IR.

quote: while its ASCII twin was still refused
defect: Adding a UTF-8 check to the cycle scan changed the diagnostic for non-ASCII twins of re-entrant fixtures, so they no longer matched their ASCII twins.
rule: For inputs that differ only in character class, assert the same diagnostic code; re-run every twin pair after adding a check to any reader.
catch_how: Generate ASCII and non-ASCII twins of each fixture and compare the diagnostic codes they draw.

quote: The library crashes the process with an unrecoverable stack overflow
defect: A schema whose $ref names its own $anchor crashes the process with a stack overflow in the resolver, reachable on main, and only a misreading had refused one shape of it.
rule: Before relying on a dependency to refuse an input class, probe that input class directly; a refusal that holds only by accident of another bug is not a bound.
catch_how: Fuzz the compile with self-referencing anchor refs and run it under a bounded stack.

quote: The doc comment on `Scope.InternalPointer` said the library "happens to reject" anchor fragments.
defect: The doc comment claimed the resolver rejects anchor fragments, but it resolves some of them.
rule: A comment stating what a dependency does with an input must cite a probe of that input; 'happens to' claims are version-bound and wrong for some inputs.
catch_how: Run the dependency on each input the comment names and compare with the comment's claim.

quote: a union variant whose `$ref` fragment is not UTF-8 was hinted `empty`
defect: The naming layer dropped invalid bytes from a reference fragment and returned an empty hint for a non-empty reference.
rule: A naming or sanitising function that drops input bytes must never return an empty result for a non-empty input; fall back to the raw text.
catch_how: Feed each ill-formed name through every namer and assert the output is non-empty and derived from the input.

quote: name the base even when the overlay wrote every keyword in them is #534
defect: Combined if/then/else, contains and unevaluated entries stay attributed to the base even when the overlay wrote every keyword in them.
rule: When a change leaves a known-wrong answer in place, make the test pin that answer in a row that names the open issue, so the fix flips the row.
catch_how: grep test tables for rows that name an open issue and confirm each pins the answer the issue describes.

quote: so they were handed the base document's raw source index and built every
defect: The annotation readers, sitting below the lowering context, built provenance from the base document's raw source index, so overlay-added extensions and keywords were attributed to the base.
rule: When a value depends on context such as overlay attribution, do not let lower layers read the raw input; inject a locator and remove the raw type from the signature so the mistake does not compile.
catch_how: Compile an overlay that adds one record of each kind and assert each record's provenance names the overlay.

quote: `irverify.Verify` passed a string-kinded value
defect: Verify accepted a string-kinded value carrying a list payload, and any other kind paired with a payload its kind does not select.
rule: For each kind-discriminated value, verify that only the payload the kind selects is set, and guard the carrier list against the fields the source declares to hold a value.
catch_how: Plant a stray payload on every kind and expect a violation for each.

quote: so before this nothing reported one on a number value.
defect: checkBigVals skipped an empty Num as unused, so a number value with no digits was never reported.
rule: A check that skips an empty value as unused must be re-examined for each kind where empty is the only malformed case; list each kind's empty meaning.
catch_how: Give each value kind an empty payload and assert a finding for every kind where empty is invalid.

quote: passes an operation bound to no channel while it rejects one bound to an undeclared channel
defect: pass.Validate rejects a dangling channel reference but not an empty one, so the CLI accepts an operation bound to no channel.
rule: When two checkers enforce one rule, run both over the same empty, dangling and valid inputs and diff their verdicts before claiming the rule is covered.
catch_how: Run pass.Validate and irverify on an operation with an empty channel ID and on one with an undeclared ID, then compare.

quote: The pass comment that claimed an empty channel was reported elsewhere now says which
defect: A pass comment claimed an empty channel was reported by another checker, which was not true for pass.Validate.
rule: A comment claiming that another checker reports a case must be verified by running that checker on the case.
catch_how: Run each checker the comment names on the case the comment describes.

quote: document spelled that reuse decided whether it compiled:
defect: The same operation reuse exited 0 or 1 depending on whether it was spelled as a $ref or as a YAML alias.
rule: Two spellings of the same reuse (a $ref and a YAML alias) must yield identical severities and exit codes; diff the diagnostics of every spelling pair.
catch_how: Compile each spelling pair of one reuse and diff the severity, code and exit code.

quote: reported whichever claim was lowered second
defect: The operationId finding was placed on whichever claim lowered second, so a $ref reuse was flagged order-dependently by morphic-harness.
rule: A finding's location must derive from the declaration itself, never from lowering order; check it with a two-order diff of the diagnostics.
catch_how: Lower the document with declarations swapped and diff the full diagnostic list including locations.
covered_ref: Order-dependence needs a two-order diff.

quote: A self-reference spelled through a directory, like `./spec.yaml#/...`, is read
defect: A self-reference spelled with a directory prefix is treated as another document, so it shares no identity with the plain spelling and reports a false conflict.
rule: Normalise a document's own path before comparing references to it; a self-reference spelled with ./ or a directory must resolve to the same identity as the plain form.
catch_how: Compile the same self-reference in each spelling and compare the claims and diagnostics.

quote: By node alone, that reuse would be an error naming one pointer on both sides.
defect: Grouping declarations by YAML node alone would have reported a self-file-name reuse as a conflict naming one pointer on both sides.
rule: Group items by every identity they can carry (node and resolved declaration pointer), and make a single-key grouping a failing test case.
catch_how: Add a fixture that reuses one declaration through a self-file-name reference and a plain reference, and assert no conflict is reported.

quote: Reading the `paths` mapping pair by pair for every claim
defect: Scanning the paths mapping pair by pair for every operationId claim would have made the walk quadratic in the number of paths.
rule: Inside a per-item loop, index any mapping the loop reads rather than scanning it, and measure the loop at 20,000 items.
catch_how: Time the compile of a document with 20,000 paths; if the time grows quadratically with paths, rewrite the lookup.

quote: #511 proposed two fields. It missed the third kind
defect: The issue's two-field proposal for provenance missed the IR-space IDs pass.Validate writes, which a typed RFC 6901 pointer field would have rejected.
rule: Before typing a field from a proposal, grep every writer of the field and enumerate the value shapes it actually receives; a type that rejects a real writer's output is wrong.
catch_how: List every assignment to the field and assert each output parses under the new type.

quote: The CLI printed a position as a URI fragment (`spec.yaml#5:1`, #509)
defect: The CLI rendered a line:col position in the syntax of a URI fragment, which reads as an RFC 6901 pointer.
rule: Render each locator kind in its own syntax; a fragment marker may introduce only an RFC 6901 pointer.
catch_how: Render each locator kind and check the output against that kind's grammar.

quote: stops at an unrelated error before the oracle runs, so it tests nothing
defect: The order oracle's line-and-column table case stops at an unrelated error before the oracle runs, so the case tests nothing.
rule: Before counting a fixture as coverage for a check, confirm the check runs on it and not an earlier error.
catch_how: Add a probe that makes the check's assertion fail and confirm the fixture turns red.
covered_ref: A negative fixture must be reachable.

quote: A refused compile returns no `Document`, so the CLI has no source table
defect: A refused compile returns no Document, so the CLI prints locations bare, without the source table that would name the file.
rule: A refusal path must still carry source locators for its diagnostics; never let the refusal result drop the source table.
catch_how: Compile a refused spec through the CLI and check that every diagnostic's location names its source file.

quote: A shared primitive records `{source: 0}` with no pointer
defect: A shared primitive's provenance has a source but no locator, so --explain names the whole document as its node.
rule: A provenance with a source but no locator names the whole document; a shared node must record a locator or be given none.
catch_how: Run --explain on the shared primitive's node and check the reported location.

quote: which would always fail as `Equal` and always pass as `NotEqual`
defect: testify Equal and NotEqual between a string and a jsontext.Pointer always fail and always pass respectively, so such assertions tested nothing.
rule: When a field changes type, scan test assertions on that field for Equal or NotEqual calls with mismatched argument types, since they fail or pass regardless of the value.
catch_how: Run a type-checked scan (go/types) over test files for assert calls whose argument types differ.

quote: no pointer. An empty pointer is the RFC 6901 pointer to the whole document, so the IR said the root
defect: A shared primitive with no single place in the source was interned with an empty pointer, which is the RFC 6901 pointer to the whole document, so --explain named the root as declaring every primitive.
rule: Before reusing a sentinel locator value (an empty pointer, zero index) for a node, check whether a consumer reads that value as 'the whole input'; give nodes with no single place their own sentinel and make the root query exclude them.
catch_how: Compile a spec with shared primitives, run the explain or lookup at the root coordinate, and inspect which node it names and where that node is declared.

quote: was credited with `not` but not with the if/then/else it also wrote.
defect: A combined Unmodeled entry (if/then/else, contains, unevaluated) was attributed to the declaring schema even when the overlay wrote every keyword in it, while single-keyword entries beside it were credited to the overlay.
rule: When one output entry is assembled from several input positions, attribute it by the positions that wrote its parts, and test three cases: all parts from the overlay, all from the base, and a mix where the first or the last part comes from the other document.
catch_how: Write an overlay that supplies every keyword of a combined construct and check the Source of the resulting entry and of the error that stands in for it when one keyword fails to convert.

quote: recognized `items`, `additionalProperties` and `contentSchema` by spelling alone, so a
defect: A position's name was guessed from its pointer's tail, so a property or patternProperties key spelled like a keyword was read as the keyword and its children were named differently depending on which lowering reached them first.
rule: Order-dependence needs a two-order diff. When deriving a role from a pointer, walk the structure from a known root and treat each map key as a key, never by its spelling in the last token.
catch_how: Two-order diff over a fixture whose property is named like a keyword, with a $ref aimed at the position above it, declared in both orders.
covered_ref: Order-dependence needs a two-order diff

quote: had nothing for the declaration to rename when the declaration came first, so a
defect: A position whose declaration interns no node (a pure $ref) could not be renamed by the declaration when a later reference had already named it after the $ref target, so the name depended on which came first.
rule: Order-dependence needs a two-order diff. When a declaration produces no node at a location a later reference may populate, record the declared name for that location so the later population takes it.
catch_how: Two-order diff with a pure-$ref target declared, reached by a reference from another path, in both orders.
covered_ref: Order-dependence needs a two-order diff

quote: took the pointer's last token
defect: A union variant or allOf branch that names a position took the pointer's last token ('0', 'items') as its name instead of the name of the node it holds ('variant_0', 'a_item').
rule: A name taken from the last token of a pointer is right only when that token names the node; name a node after what it holds, and check indexed and keyword-like tokens in union variants and composition branches.
catch_how: Compile a union whose variants point at an array index and at a property and assert the variant names in the IR.

quote: so the case passed without asking its question.
defect: A table case asserted only that the outcome was not OutcomeOrderDependent, which an earlier oracle's outcome also satisfies, so the case passed without ever reaching the order oracle it was written for.
rule: A check that runs is not a check that reaches. A table test must assert the one outcome its case exists to reach, not a negation that an earlier stage can satisfy, and must fail when the case stops reaching that stage.
catch_how: Make the fixture stop earlier (for example add an error diagnostic) and confirm the case turns red rather than green.
covered_ref: A check that runs is not a check that reaches.

quote: A document an external `$ref` names never passed through that
defect: The anchor release applied to the source document only; external documents read by the resolver itself skipped it, so anchored operations and responses in them were silently missing from the IR with exit 0.
rule: Sweep every site of the mechanism before closing it. When a guard or transformation is applied to the root input, check each other input path (external references, caches, second readers) reaches the same guard.
catch_how: Put an anchored operation in an external document, compile with external references allowed, and check the operation appears in the IR.
covered_ref: Sweep every site of the mechanism before closing it.

quote: With the refusal unwired, a folded-entry fixture
defect: Lifting the anchor skip let a recursive anchor on a folded entry recurse without end, and without the refusal the fixture grew past 57 GB RSS, so the change needed an explicit refusal to stay bounded.
rule: Bounded everything. Before removing a guard that incidentally stopped a recursion or a growth, add an explicit bound or refusal in the same change, and run the input the guard covered under a memory or time limit.
catch_how: Run the recursive-anchor fixture through the new path under a memory limit and a timeout and confirm it terminates with a diagnostic.
covered_ref: Bounded everything.

quote: dropped from `Document.Sources` while its `overlay-origin-incomplete` warning named index 1.
defect: On the success path an overlay applied past the attribution budget was dropped from the Document's source table while its warning still named source index 1, so a diagnostic pointed at an index the table did not hold.
rule: Sweep every site of the mechanism before closing it. When a source table is built on two paths (success and budget-exhausted), check both populate it identically and that every index a diagnostic can name is in it.
catch_how: Compile with an overlay past the attribution budget and assert every diagnostic's source index is in Result.Sources.
covered_ref: Sweep every site of the mechanism before closing it.

quote: A set keyed by node cannot outgrow the tree, so
defect: The enters-once test compared the walk's set with the tree's node count, a bound no walk can violate, so it passed with the seen check removed and could not fail.
rule: Break what a test claims to catch. A test whose bound a derived set cannot exceed proves nothing; plant each defect the test names and confirm it turns red before the test is accepted.
catch_how: Remove the seen check (and separately let an alias walk its target unguarded) and run the test; expect red.
covered_ref: Break what a test claims to catch.

quote: The timing test failed CI on noise.
defect: A wall-clock ratio test allowed 3 against a linear-versus-quadratic separation of 2, so a race-detector run on a shared CI machine crossed the allowance and failed the gate on noise.
rule: A timing assertion needs its expected separation well above run-to-run noise: widen the gap between the two growth rates, not the allowance, and measure the ratio's distribution over repeated runs including under -race.
catch_how: Run the timing test about 40 times, default and -race, and report median and maximum ratio against the allowance before pushing.

quote: The rebuild replaces what a reference built, not what it reported.
defect: When a declaration rebuilds a node a reference built, the diagnostics and Unmodeled entries the superseded build recorded (default, readOnly, writeOnly) stayed, so the report described entries the rebuilt document no longer holds.

quote: so an unrelated respelled `$ref` turned that compile's

quote: Each of those was superlinear in an earlier revision of this branch.

defect: A chained failure quoted a stopped internal #/components/... reference without its document, so the quote read as naming a component of the source.

defect: The architecture rules matched package names syntactically, so an aliased import of ir or compile was not policed and an unrelated package named compile was falsely flagged.
