catch_how: Plant a violation under an aliased import and a clean use of an unrelated package named like the guarded one; both must give the expected result.

quote: Three comments and §3.1 said agreement with the recorded pointer is the
defect: Three comments and the design doc claimed pointer agreement was the only way irverify catches a lost separator, which the new namespace check disproved.
rule: When a new detector covers a case an earlier comment called the only way, grep for words like 'only' and 'only way' near the old detector and rewrite each one in the same change.
catch_how: grep the docs and source comments for 'only way' or 'only' next to the detector's name and check each claim against the new detector.

quote: §3.1 no longer says a group's name is part of its ID right after
defect: The design doc stated that a group's name was part of its ID directly after defining the ID formats, contradicting the rule that names are presentation.
rule: After writing a normative doc section, re-read each sentence that names an identity component and check it against the invariant that defines what identity is made of.
catch_how: Read the new doc section beside the invariant it cites and check each identity-component sentence for a name that should not be part of the ID.

quote: Each of these held only by accident; widening or dropping it left every
defect: Three special cases (the primitive-namespace exemption, the kind-table completeness, and the unknown-kind declaration) had no test that failed when they were widened or dropped.
rule: For each exemption or special case in a check, add a test that fails when the exemption is widened or removed, not only the test that exercises the normal path.
catch_how: Widen each exemption and remove each special case one at a time, and confirm a test named for it goes red.
covered_ref: Break what a test claims to catch

quote: null list verified clean, so a second producer could write one and the
defect: A declaration key holding an empty or null namespace list verified clean, although the canonical form forbids it and two producers could then emit differing declarations.
rule: For each canonical-form rule, test every degenerate value (empty, null, absent) of each collection it governs, not only the populated case.
catch_how: Build a document declaring an empty list and a null list for each kind and confirm the verifier reports each one.

quote: different filters. That derivation is the basis of the guarantee that a
defect: Two tests each derived the set of namespaces a document uses with slightly different filters, so the guarantee that the declaration equals actual use could drift apart silently.
rule: When a guarantee rests on a derivation, compute it in one shared helper and have every test call that helper rather than re-deriving it.
catch_how: grep the test packages for the same derivation (for example a filter over the same declared IDs) and check that all copies call one helper.

quote: No test said which one irverify enforces; replacing the comparison with a
defect: The canonical sort order of namespace lists (UTF-8 byte order) was not pinned by any test, so swapping to UTF-16 ordering left every test green.
rule: For every ordering a canonical form specifies, add a case whose inputs sort differently under the plausible wrong orders, and confirm the test fails under each.
catch_how: Replace the comparison with each alternative order (UTF-16, locale) and confirm a test reddens.

quote: registry, where the loop it replaced returned an empty slice. A caller
defect: Rewriting Registry.Formats with slices.SortedFunc changed an empty registry's result from a non-nil empty slice to nil, which changes JSON encoding from [] to null, and the initial change claimed no caller could tell.
rule: When a rewrite replaces a loop with a standard-library helper, compare the zero-result representation (nil versus empty) with the original and check every consumer that encodes or distinguishes it.
catch_how: Call the rewritten function on an empty input and marshal the result to JSON; compare with the output of the original function.

quote: The ordering test registers three formats, which the registry's map hands
defect: The ordering test used three formats, so a dropped version tiebreak in the sort passed it about one run in five and the test did not check what it claimed.
rule: When a test's input order comes from a map or other unordered source, run the test against a deliberately broken comparator many times to confirm it fails each time; a test that passes by chance is not a check.
catch_how: Drop the tiebreak in the comparator and run the test 100 times; count the failures.
covered_ref: Break what a test claims to catch

quote: the registry unsorted left every test green while the printed node changed
defect: The explain command's choice of node at a shared coordinate depended on unsorted map iteration, and no test pinned that order, so the printed node changed between runs.
rule: For every output selected from an unordered collection when several candidates share a key, add a case with those candidates and assert the chosen one.
catch_how: Swap the iteration order (sorted versus reversed versus unsorted) of the collection and confirm a test asserts the printed result changes or stays fixed as intended.
covered_ref: Order-dependence needs a two-order diff

quote: edge, reddened TestLoweringRecursion_IsOnlyTheKnownCycles and nothing
defect: Skipping closure bodies or counting a field as an edge was caught only by the real-tree assertion, so a tree that stopped containing such a construct would let the regression through silently.
rule: For each branch of a graph or traversal builder, add a planted case that fails when that branch is mutated, rather than relying on the real tree to exercise it.
catch_how: Mutate each branch of the builder one at a time and run only the planted table; each mutation must redden it.
covered_ref: Break what a test claims to catch

quote: that explained a failure mode of the removed resolver, a lookup by
defect: A test comment kept explaining a failure mode of the hand-written resolver that the typed call graph can no longer have.
rule: When removing an implementation, grep the tests and comments that describe its failure modes and delete or rewrite each one in the same change.
catch_how: grep the test files for the removed function's name and for words like 'resolver' or 'lookup by' and read each hit against the new implementation.

quote: The recipe mints a profile path with mktemp, but recipe lines run without
defect: The Makefile recipe minted its profile path with mktemp without checking the result, so a failed mktemp left the path empty and the whole suite ran with an empty -coverprofile before the gate reported anything.
rule: In a Makefile recipe a failing command does not stop the recipe unless it is checked: after any command whose output a later line depends on, end the recipe explicitly when that command fails.
catch_how: Run the recipe with a stand-in command that exits non-zero for the step that produces the value, and confirm the recipe stops before the step that consumes it.

quote: The only test of the cap listed 30 gaps, which left the count line's
defect: The only test of the gap-listing cap used 30 gaps, so the cap's boundary and the count line's threshold were unobserved and off-by-one mutants of both passed.
rule: For any cap or threshold, add cases exactly at the boundary, one below and one above, and compare the whole output, so an off-by-one mutant of the comparison reddens a test.
catch_how: Change each comparison by one (>= for >, a cap plus or minus one) and confirm some test fails for every change.

quote: none named the coverage gate's judge added alongside it.
defect: The layout listings in CLAUDE.md, README.md and docs/architecture.md named the sibling command cmd/morphic-harness but not the new cmd/morphic-covergate, so the listings were incomplete.
rule: When adding a package or command, grep the docs for a sibling that they already enumerate and add the new entry to every listing that names the sibling.
catch_how: Run grep over *.md for the sibling's path, and check each hit lists the new package or command too.

quote: cover.ParseProfiles merges repeated blocks after sorting on a block's
defect: The known limit that ParseProfiles can leave copies of blocks sharing a start unmerged was stated only in the PR body, not beside the call that relies on the merge.
rule: A limit of a library call the code relies on must be written in the code beside that call, not only in the PR body or a commit message.
catch_how: Read the call site cold and check that every known limit of the callee is stated there, not only in the PR description.
covered_ref: A limitation that is deliberately out of scope must be stated in the code and in the PR body

quote: no test CI runs could tell it from the check it replaced
defect: The grid test could not distinguish the rooted-path fix from the replaced '..' check on any host CI runs, so reverting the fix left the whole package green.
rule: When a fix changes behaviour only on a platform CI does not run, inject that platform's reading as an input and test it on the current host, then revert the fix and confirm the test reddens.
catch_how: Reinstate the replaced check and run the package tests on the CI platform; if the suite stays green, the test does not reach the changed branch.
covered_ref: Plant the defect and watch it go red.

quote: SameDocument's comment named a path climbing out of the working
defect: The SameDocument doc comment still described the old '..' climbing check after the check was replaced by filepath.IsLocal, so it no longer described which paths read the working directory.
rule: When a mechanism is replaced, reread every doc comment that describes its old behaviour and rewrite it for the new mechanism before pushing.
catch_how: Grep the changed package's comments for the old check's key phrases and for the removed identifier, and read each hit against the new code.

quote: sameAnchor's comment gave C:a as the drive-relative example, but IsURL
defect: The doc comment's drive-relative example C:a is read by IsURL as a URL, so SameDocument never reaches the check the comment describes for it.
rule: Before citing an example input in a doc comment, run that literal through the function and confirm it takes the branch the comment says it takes.
catch_how: Call the function with the exact example literal under a probe that reports which branch ran, and compare it with the comment.

quote: DefaultOf returned one could not change a result: replacing it with
defect: A nil guard before assigning the schema default could not change any result, because the carrier was always nil at that point, so its replacement by true survived the suite.
rule: A conditional whose outcome cannot change any result is dead code: delete it rather than keep it, and treat a surviving mutant on a guard as proof that the guard is dead.
catch_how: Replace each if-guard with true and with false in turn, and confirm some test fails for each; a guard that survives both is dead.
covered_ref: Plant the defect and watch it go red.

quote: fillParamDefault no longer exists: fillParamSchema assigns the value
defect: A comment on paramHoldsResidue named fillParamDefault, a function the refactor had removed, so the comment pointed at nothing.
rule: After deleting or renaming a function, grep the comments and docs for its old name and retarget every hit before pushing.
catch_how: Grep the whole tree, comments included, for each identifier the diff removes or renames.

quote: The table restated the grammar by hand, so a change in the library's
defect: The IsIndex table restated the library's token grammar by hand, so it agreed with the implementation while both could be wrong against the library.
rule: A table test that claims to follow an authority (a library, a spec) must check the implementation against that authority itself, not against a restatement of its rule written in the test.
catch_how: Replace the implementation with a plausible-but-wrong variant and confirm the table fails; if the table only encodes the author's own reading, it still passes.

quote: an IsIndex bounded by strconv.Atoi passed the earlier table.
defect: The index-token table had no inputs beyond the int range or ending in a line break, so an IsIndex bounded by strconv.Atoi passed although the library types those tokens differently.
rule: When a parse-equivalence table checks a helper against a library, include inputs at the representation's limits (overflowing numbers, trailing line breaks) because a parser helper diverges from the library at exactly those edges.
catch_how: Run the helper and the library on overflow and trailing-newline inputs and diff their answers before trusting the table.

quote: single call, and nothing asserted it: dropping the call left the suite
defect: The diagnostics a hoisted scalar reports for its constraints were never asserted, so dropping the reporting call left the whole suite green.
rule: Each diagnostic a helper emits needs a case that triggers it; delete the emitting call under a probe and confirm some test fails.
catch_how: Remove each diagnostic-emitting call in turn and run the suite; any call whose removal stays green has no test reaching it.
covered_ref: Plant the defect and watch it go red.

quote: No test fed pointerOf a key that is no UTF-8, so spelling it through
defect: No test gave pointerOf a key that is not valid UTF-8, so spelling the token through AppendToken, which rewrites such bytes as U+FFFD, went unnoticed.
rule: For a function whose output depends on byte or encoding edge cases, add an input that is not valid UTF-8 and check the output against the library's own behaviour on the same bytes.
catch_how: Feed the function a non-UTF-8 key and compare its output with the library's escaper; replacing the library call with a lossy variant must redden a test.
covered_ref: an input class no committed fixture produces, is enough

quote: No test covered a webhook's own callbacks or a callback operation's
defect: No test covered a webhook's own callbacks or a callback operation's inferred marker, so removing either from its route left the suite green.
rule: When several routes share one loop, add a test per route for each per-route setting (callbacks, flags, markers) and remove each setting in turn to confirm a test reddens.
catch_how: Drop each per-route assignment in the shared loop, one at a time, and run the suite; every drop must redden a named test.
covered_ref: Plant the defect and watch it go red.

quote: schema at either site went unnoticed. A test now holds both.
defect: Handing internAlias no schema at the two sites where it is the only node carrying the bounds went unnoticed, because no test covered those call sites.
rule: When a helper reads a value from a parameter the caller supplies, test the caller with that argument removed at each call site, not only the helper in isolation.
catch_how: Pass the zero or nil value at each call site in turn and confirm some test fails for each.

quote: The overlay test's comment named lowerComponentSchema as where a
defect: The overlay test's comment named lowerComponentSchema as the reader of a component schema's kept modifier, but the read happens in hoistDeclarationHome, which is the call the test actually depends on.
rule: A test comment that names where a value is read must name the call whose removal makes the test fail; verify by removing each candidate call in turn.
catch_how: Delete each call the comment could mean, one at a time, and see which deletion reddens the test.

quote: The hand-written escape this walk used said why it was not jsontext's
defect: Replacing the hand-written escape with the library escaper dropped the comment explaining why the hand-written escape existed, which is what stops a later change from reverting to jsontext.AppendToken.
rule: When replacing a hand-written construct with a library call, keep the comment that says why the hand-written one existed, since that reason is what stops a later revert.
catch_how: Diff the comments on the replaced lines and confirm the rationale survived the swap.
covered_ref: comments explain *why*, not what.

quote: One commit subject on the branch, `hoist a content scalar through hoistFormatScalar`, is 77 characters, over the 72-character cap.
defect: A pushed branch carried a commit subject of 77 characters, over the 72-character cap, because the length was not measured before the first push.
rule: Measure every commit subject's length (awk length over the branch's log) before the first push, since a pushed subject cannot be shortened without rewriting the branch.
catch_how: Run git log --format=%s origin/main..HEAD piped through awk 'length($0) > 72' before pushing.
covered_ref: a commit subject over the 72-char cap

quote: Neither mutant reddened any test in the module.
defect: The merge-key test checked only the quoted and plain spellings, so a predicate reading only the tag, and a call handed the alias-resolved key, both passed every test.
rule: For a predicate with several conditions, mutate each condition and each caller input separately, and confirm a test fails for every mutant; a test covering only some conditions misses the rest.
catch_how: Build one mutant per condition (drop it, invert it) and per caller input (pass the pre-transformed value), and confirm each reddens a named test.
covered_ref: Plant the defect and watch it go red.

quote: `detect.go` models the unmarshaller but tests the tag alone, so `!!merge openapi: 3.1.0` is declined as an unrecognized format.
defect: detect.go tests only the tag when deciding a merge key, so a document whose version key is written with the merge tag is wrongly declined as an unrecognized format, while the library accepts it.
rule: After replacing one copy of a library rule with the library call, sweep every other copy of the same rule and test each one against the spellings the library accepts.
catch_how: For each spelling the library parses, run every sibling copy of the rule and compare its answer with the library's.

quote: test(ir): stop a local shadowing the go/types import
defect: A local identifier in a test file shadowed the go/types import name, so later uses of the package in that scope would not compile or would silently refer to the local.
rule: Never name a local variable after a package imported in the same file; a local that shadows an import breaks every later reference to that package in its scope.
catch_how: Grep each changed file for locals whose names equal an imported package name, or run a linter with import-shadowing checks enabled before pushing.
covered_ref: never shadow builtins or imports

quote: StringConsts promised declaration order but sorted by token.Pos.
defect: StringConsts ordered constants by token.Pos, which orders files by whichever concurrent parse finished first, so the order differed from load to load.
rule: When sources are parsed concurrently, never order results by token.Pos; sort by a stable key such as file name then offset, and verify the order by repeating the load and comparing.
catch_how: Load the same package many times in a loop and diff the returned order; a result that varies between runs is nondeterministic.

quote: A wildcard among several patterns that matched no package was
defect: A pattern matching no package was dropped silently by the go command and the loader, so the load returned fewer packages than requested with no error.
rule: A loader or test helper must fail when its result is smaller than its input; compare the requested and returned sets rather than trusting a tool's warning.
catch_how: Pass a pattern that matches nothing alongside a valid one and assert the load returns an error.

quote: A file the current build leaves out was not read. A declaration in
defect: A file excluded by the current build configuration was not read, so a declaration in it was invisible to the checks and they passed without it.
rule: A source loader must refuse any production file the build excludes instead of skipping it; a checker that reads less than the tree reports clean on code it never saw.
catch_how: Add a declaration in a file under a non-matching build tag and assert the loader errors and names the file.

quote: A package with only test files loaded as an empty package, and every
defect: A package containing only test files loaded as an empty package, so every question asked of it returned an empty answer with no error.
rule: A package loader must treat a package with no production source as an error, not as an empty package whose queries silently return nothing.
catch_how: Point the loader at a directory holding only a _test.go file and assert it fails.

quote: Before, only `ir.X` selectors anywhere in the function counted, including ones in
defect: The ValueKind switch check identified switches by ir.X selector text anywhere in the function, so it was blind to aliased, converted and init-statement switches and counted arms of unrelated switches.
rule: A scanner that finds a construct must key on the type the compiler resolves (the switch tag's type), not on one syntactic spelling; test it against each spelling the language accepts.
catch_how: Plant an incomplete switch written with an alias type, a conversion arm and an init statement, and confirm the scanner flags it.

quote: One change is not carried over yet. Main widened the ValueKind
defect: Merging main resolved a conflict to the branch's narrower single-switch reader, silently dropping main's wider scope over every ValueKind switch until a later commit restored it.
rule: After merging main into a branch, re-diff each semantic change main made to files the branch touches and confirm it survived conflict resolution; a conflict resolved to one side drops the other side's change without error.
catch_how: After the merge, diff main's changes to each conflicted file against the merged result and check every semantic edit is present.

quote: read one function, enumMemberForm, in one file.
defect: The ValueKind completeness suite still read a single function in one file after main had widened the check to every ValueKind switch in the tree.
rule: When a check's scope is widened on main, apply the same widening to every branch that touches the check before merging; a test's scope is part of what it claims.
catch_how: Compare the scope of each test on the branch with the scope of the same test on main after every merge.

quote: Only the promotion walk held
defect: The conformance walk over TypeKinds lacked the guard that held the kind count to the typeDef() markers, which only the promotion walk had.
rule: When two walks implement the same mechanism, apply each guard to both and plant a violation in each walk to confirm both reddens.
catch_how: Add a variant without a kind and confirm each walk's test fails, not only one.

quote: which puts line 14 before line 6
defect: The ValueKind switch scan sorted its results by a file:line string, so line 14 sorted before line 6.
rule: Never sort by a formatted string that contains numbers; sort by the numeric fields or keep the collection's source order.
catch_how: Plant two switches in one file at lines 6 and 14 and assert the report lists them in line order.

quote: failure said only that the list should have one more item.
defect: TestCodes_MatchTheDeclaredSet compared counts, so a missing code produced a failure that named no code.
rule: A test that holds a list to a declared set should diff the members, so a failure names the missing or duplicated member rather than a count.
catch_how: Remove one declared member and read the failure text; it must name that member.

quote: Several comments still said the ir sources were parsed with go/ast; they
defect: Doc comments and test names still described the sources as parsed with go/ast after the reader had changed to type-checked reads.
rule: After changing how a source is read, grep the code and comments for the old mechanism's name (parse, go/ast) and update every mention.
catch_how: Run grep for the old mechanism's name across the package after the refactor and read each hit.

quote: The decls fixture that imports its sibling is the one in-module import
defect: A testdata fixture that imports a sibling package was an in-module import the architecture test would refuse under the package's allowlist, and it was not listed there.
rule: A testdata fixture under an architecture-tested tree that imports an in-module package is part of the import graph; list it in the allowlist or the architecture test refuses it.
catch_how: Run the architecture test over the new package and its testdata before pushing.
covered_ref: The layering is enforced by `internal/archtest`

quote: "is a Int constant" and "is not a UnmodeledReason" read badly when they
defect: Two failure messages read ungrammatically ("is a Int constant", "is not a UnmodeledReason").
rule: Read each diagnostic and assertion message as it would print, and check article agreement and phrasing before pushing.
catch_how: Force each failure message to fire and read the output aloud.

quote: trailing slash, so it is modulePrefix now and irImportPath is derived
defect: A constant named modulePath held a prefix with a trailing slash, so its name did not match its value.
rule: Name a constant for what its value actually contains; a prefix with a trailing separator is not a path.
catch_how: Read each new constant's value against its name during review.

quote: callsWalkValues matched the callee by a full-name string built from the
defect: callsWalkValues identified WalkValues by a full-name string built from the import path, which can miss a renamed or dotted import and does not identify the object.
rule: Identify a function across packages by its type-checker object (types.Object identity), never by a path-and-name string you construct.
catch_how: Test the check with a renamed import and a dotted import of the function and confirm both are matched.

quote: The predicate is now "refers to" rather than "calls", so a function that
defect: The walker predicate only matched calls, so a function that passed WalkValues on as a value was not counted as a walker.
rule: A check on call sites must also consider a function used as a value; scan for references to the symbol, not only call expressions.
catch_how: Plant a function that assigns WalkValues to a variable without calling it and confirm the check flags it.

quote: reports whether the last result is "a bool,
defect: endsInBool's doc said a defined bool type counts, but the check compares against the predeclared bool only, so the doc overstated what is accepted.
rule: When a doc comment states what a type check accepts, check whether the comparison is by identity or by name; a defined type with the same underlying kind does not satisfy a predeclared-type check.
catch_how: Pass a defined bool type to the check and confirm the doc's claim matches the result.

quote: declaredFields skipped every alias, so a field declared inside
defect: declaredFields skipped every type alias, so fields declared inside an alias of a struct literal reached none of the scans and the pins stayed green.
rule: A scanner over declarations must cover every spelling the type checker resolves, including aliases of struct literals; plant each spelling and confirm the pin reddens.
catch_how: Plant an alias of a struct literal holding an integer field and confirm the integer-field pin fails.
covered_ref: Plant the defect and watch it go red.

quote: A load refused a package for any file its build left out, so an
defect: The loader refused a package for any build-excluded file, including assembly and C files that declare nothing the checker sees.
rule: A refusal must fire only on the condition it names; exempt the file kinds the checker never reads, such as non-Go and test files.
catch_how: Add an assembly file constrained to another platform to the fixture and confirm the load still succeeds.

quote: The fixture now also holds a test file every build includes.
defect: The only test file in the fixture was one no build includes, so a loader that read test files passed every test in the package.
rule: A negative fixture must contain an instance of each input class the check claims to handle; revert the check and confirm the fixture reddens.
catch_how: Make the loader read test files and confirm a test fails; if none does, the fixture never reaches the case.
covered_ref: A negative fixture must be reachable.

quote: The case that makes the go command fail matched the full flag spelling in
defect: The test that makes the go command fail matched the full flag spelling in the tool's message, so any rewording of that message would redden it.
rule: In a test, match only the fragment the code under test controls, never the full wording of an external tool's message.
catch_how: Reword the external tool's message in a probe and confirm the test still passes for the right reason.

quote: driver reports what it chooses.
defect: A load ran through whatever external driver GOPACKAGESDRIVER or PATH supplied, so a build-system driver that listed only included files could make a left-out-file refusal lapse without a sign.
rule: A test that runs an external tool must pin the tool's mode explicitly, so its result cannot depend on the developer's environment.
catch_how: Put a fake driver on PATH that reports a subset of files and confirm the test still fails when the subset is wrong.

quote: internal/leakcheck had been missing from all three since it landed in #535
defect: internal/decls and internal/leakcheck were missing from the package layout lists in README.md, CLAUDE.md and docs/architecture.md.
rule: When a package is added, grep every document that enumerates packages and update each one; the same list is copied into several files.
catch_how: Grep the repo's docs for a sibling package's name and confirm the new package appears in each list.

quote: go/packages type-checks every package of a load whose imports are done
defect: Type-checking several packages in one load raced inside go/types when two checkers shared an imported package, failing the compiler tree's tests in a fraction of runs.
rule: When a test helper type-checks several packages in one call, run the affected packages repeatedly under -race with the gate's flags; a shared import can race inside the type checker.
catch_how: Run the affected package 50 or more times under the gate's exact flags with -race and count failures.

quote: typescript: declare error-class and resource-handle fields explicitly
defect: The TypeScript exemplars used constructor parameter properties, which do not compile under the mandated erasableSyntaxOnly setting, so the exemplars broke the guide beside them.
rule: Compile every code exemplar in a style guide under the guide's own mandated compiler flags before merging, and lint it against the guide's rules.
catch_how: Run tsc with the guide's mandated erasableSyntaxOnly setting over each exemplar file.

quote: it with the banned non-null operator
defect: The typescript-bun exemplar asserted a nullable request body with the non-null operator, which the guide bans.
rule: Lint every code exemplar in a style guide against the guide's own banned-construct list before merging.
catch_how: Grep each exemplar for every construct the guide's rules forbid and fail on any hit.

quote: Express-style (req, res, next) one the guide forbids elsewhere.
defect: The typescript-bun logging exemplar used the Express-style middleware signature that the guide forbids elsewhere, so the example taught the banned form.
rule: Check every example in a style guide for consistency with the guide's own forbidden forms, not only the rule it illustrates.
catch_how: Grep the guide's examples for each forbidden signature and confirm none appears in an example.

quote: Python dataclass field order, and fix dangling cross-references.
defect: The Python exemplars had an invalid dataclass field order that raised TypeError at class definition, and some cross-references in the guides dangled.
rule: Execute every code exemplar in a style guide and resolve every cross-reference link before merging a guide.
catch_how: Import or run each Python exemplar file and check each internal link target exists.

quote: Reconcile duplicated running examples (Kotlin Result and RequestStep,
defect: Running examples were duplicated across chapters and had drifted apart (Kotlin Result and RequestStep, Go recursion and channel-direction guidance).
rule: When one concept appears in several chapters, keep one canonical example and link to it rather than repeating copies that can drift apart.
catch_how: Grep the guide family for each running example's type name and confirm one defining copy exists.
